     2→ * useImageEditOrchestrator
     3→ *
     4→ * Composes all image-edit mode hooks (inpainting, magic edit, reposition, img2img)
     5→ * and builds the ImageEditContext value. Extracted from ImageLightbox to keep it
     6→ * under 400 lines.
     7→ *
     8→ * Inputs: media, variant state, edit-settings persistence, lora management, upscale state.
     9→ * Outputs: imageEditValue (for context), mode flags, and generation handlers.
    10→ */
    11→
    12→import { useMemo, useCallback } from 'react';
    13→import type { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';
    14→import type { ImageEditState } from '../contexts/ImageEditContext';
    15→import type { EditAdvancedSettings, EditMode, LoraMode, QwenEditModel } from '../model/editSettingsTypes';
    16→import type { UseLoraManagerReturn } from '@/shared/hooks/useLoraManager';
    17→import type { LoraModel } from '@/shared/components/LoraSelectorModal';
    18→import type { EditMode as InpaintingEditMode } from './inpainting/types';
    19→
    20→import {
    21→  useInpainting,
    22→} from './useInpainting';
    23→import { useEditSettingsSync } from './persistence/useEditSettingsSync';
    24→import { useMagicEditMode } from './useMagicEditMode';
    25→import { useRepositionMode } from './useRepositionMode';
    26→import { useImg2ImgMode } from './useImg2ImgMode';
    27→import { buildImageEditStateValue } from '@/tools/edit-images/model/buildImageEditStateValue';
    28→
    29→// ============================================================================
    30→// Props
    31→// ============================================================================
    32→
    33→interface UseImageEditOrchestratorProps {
    34→  // Media & project context
    35→  mediaContext: {
    36→    media: GenerationRow;
    37→    selectedProjectId: string | null;
    38→    actualGenerationId: string | null;
    39→    shotId?: string;
    40→    toolTypeOverride?: string;
    41→    initialActive: boolean;
    42→    thumbnailUrl?: string;
    43→  };
    44→
    45→  // Image display context
    46→  displayContext: {
    47→    imageDimensions: { width: number; height: number } | null;
    48→    imageContainerRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
    49→    effectiveImageUrl: string;
    50→  };
    51→
    52→  // Variant state context (from useSharedLightboxState)
    53→  variantContext: {
    54→  activeVariant: {
    55→    id?: string | null;
    56→    location?: string | null;
    57→    thumbnail_url?: string | null;
    58→    params?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
    59→  } | null;
    60→  setActiveVariantId: (id: string) => void;
    61→  refetchVariants: () => void;
    62→  };
    63→
    64→  // Edit settings persistence context (from useEditSettingsPersistence)
    65→  settingsContext: {
    66→    loraMode: LoraMode;
    67→    setLoraMode: (mode: LoraMode) => void;
    68→    customLoraUrl: string;
    69→    setCustomLoraUrl: (url: string) => void;
    70→    prompt: string;
    71→    setPrompt: (prompt: string) => void;
    72→    numGenerations: number;
    73→    setNumGenerations: (num: number) => void;
    74→    img2imgStrength: number;
    75→    setImg2imgStrength: (strength: number) => void;
    76→    img2imgEnablePromptExpansion: boolean;
    77→    setImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion: (enabled: boolean) => void;
    78→    img2imgPrompt: string;
    79→    setImg2imgPrompt: (prompt: string) => void;
    80→    img2imgPromptHasBeenSet: boolean;
    81→    editModeLoras: Array<{ url: string; strength: number }> | undefined;
    82→    createAsGeneration: boolean;
    83→    setCreateAsGeneration: (value: boolean) => void;
    84→    advancedSettings: EditAdvancedSettings;
    85→    setAdvancedSettings: (updates: Partial<EditAdvancedSettings>) => void;
    86→    qwenEditModel: QwenEditModel;
    87→    setQwenEditModel: (model: QwenEditModel) => void;
    88→    editMode: EditMode;
    89→    setEditMode: (mode: EditMode) => void;
    90→    isReady: boolean;
    91→    hasPersistedSettings: boolean;
    92→  };
    93→
    94→  // LoRA context
    95→  loraContext: {
    96→    effectiveEditModeLoras: Array<{ url: string; strength: number }> | undefined;
    97→    availableLoras?: LoraModel[];
    98→  };
    99→}
   100→
   101→// ============================================================================
   102→// Return Type
   103→// ============================================================================
   104→
   105→interface UseImageEditOrchestratorReturn {
   106→  // Context value (pass to ImageEditProvider)
   107→  imageEditValue: ImageEditState;
   108→
   109→  // Mode state (for layout, panel, and shell decisions)
   110→  isInpaintMode: boolean;
   111→  isMagicEditMode: boolean;
   112→  isSpecialEditMode: boolean;
   113→  editMode: EditMode;
   114→
   115→  // Mode entry/exit (for panel mode restore and shared state)
   116→  handleEnterMagicEditMode: () => void;
   117→  handleExitMagicEditMode: () => void;
   118→
   119→  // Generation handlers (passed to EditModePanel)
   120→  handleUnifiedGenerate: () => Promise<void>;
   121→  handleGenerateAnnotatedEdit: () => Promise<void>;
   122→  handleGenerateReposition: () => Promise<void>;
   123→  handleSaveAsVariant: () => Promise<void>;
   124→  handleGenerateImg2Img: () => Promise<void>;
   125→
   126→  // Img2Img LoRA manager (passed to EditModePanel)
   127→  img2imgLoraManager: UseLoraManagerReturn;
   128→
   129→}
   130→
   131→// ============================================================================
   132→// Hook
   133→// ============================================================================
   134→
   135→export function useImageEditOrchestrator({
   136→  mediaContext,
   137→  displayContext,
   138→  variantContext,
   139→  settingsContext,
   140→  loraContext,
   141→}: UseImageEditOrchestratorProps): UseImageEditOrchestratorReturn {
   142→  const {
   143→    media,
   144→    selectedProjectId,
   145→    actualGenerationId,
   146→    shotId,
   147→    toolTypeOverride,
   148→    initialActive,
   149→    thumbnailUrl,
   150→  } = mediaContext;
   151→  const {
   152→    imageDimensions,
   153→    imageContainerRef,
   154→    effectiveImageUrl,
   155→  } = displayContext;
   156→  const {
   157→    activeVariant,
   158→    setActiveVariantId,
   159→    refetchVariants,
   160→  } = variantContext;
   161→  const {
   162→    effectiveEditModeLoras,
   163→    availableLoras,
   164→  } = loraContext;
   165→
   166→  const {
   167→    loraMode, setLoraMode,
   168→    customLoraUrl, setCustomLoraUrl,
   169→    prompt: persistedPrompt, setPrompt: setPersistedPrompt,
   170→    numGenerations: persistedNumGenerations, setNumGenerations: setPersistedNumGenerations,
   171→    img2imgStrength: persistedImg2imgStrength, setImg2imgStrength: setPersistedImg2imgStrength,
   172→    img2imgEnablePromptExpansion: persistedImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion,
   173→    setImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion: setPersistedImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion,
   174→    img2imgPrompt: persistedImg2imgPrompt, setImg2imgPrompt: setPersistedImg2imgPrompt,
   175→    img2imgPromptHasBeenSet: persistedImg2imgPromptHasBeenSet,
   176→    createAsGeneration, setCreateAsGeneration,
   177→    advancedSettings, setAdvancedSettings,
   178→    qwenEditModel, setQwenEditModel,
   179→    editMode: persistedEditMode, setEditMode: setPersistedEditMode,
   180→    isReady: isEditSettingsReady,
   181→    hasPersistedSettings,
   182→  } = settingsContext;
   183→
   184→  const toInpaintingEditMode = useCallback((mode: EditMode): InpaintingEditMode => {
   185→    if (mode === 'inpaint' || mode === 'annotate' || mode === 'text') {
   186→      return mode;
   187→    }
   188→    return 'text';
   189→  }, []);
   190→
   191→  // ========================================
   192→  // INPAINTING HOOK
   193→  // ========================================
   194→
   195→  const inpaintingHook = useInpainting({
   196→    media,
   197→    selectedProjectId,
   198→    shotId,
   199→    toolTypeOverride,
   200→    isVideo: false,
   201→    imageContainerRef,
   202→    imageDimensions,
   203→    handleExitInpaintMode: () => {},
   204→    loras: effectiveEditModeLoras,
   205→    activeVariantId: activeVariant?.id,
   206→    activeVariantLocation: activeVariant?.location,
   207→    createAsGeneration,
   208→    advancedSettings,
   209→    qwenEditModel,
   210→    imageUrl: activeVariant?.location || effectiveImageUrl,
   211→    thumbnailUrl: thumbnailUrl || media.thumbUrl,
   212→    initialEditMode: toInpaintingEditMode(persistedEditMode),
   213→  });
   214→
   215→  // Destructure only what's needed for inter-hook wiring, settings sync, and return value
   216→  const {
   217→    isInpaintMode, editMode, setIsInpaintMode, setEditMode,
   218→    brushStrokes, inpaintPrompt, inpaintNumGenerations,
   219→    setInpaintPrompt, setInpaintNumGenerations,
   220→    handleEnterInpaintMode, handleGenerateInpaint, handleGenerateAnnotatedEdit,
   221→  } = inpaintingHook;
   222→
   223→  // ========================================
   224→  // EDIT SETTINGS SYNC
   225→  // ========================================
   226→
   227→  useEditSettingsSync({
   228→    actualGenerationId: actualGenerationId ?? undefined,
   229→    isEditSettingsReady,
   230→    hasPersistedSettings,
   231→    persistedEditMode,
   232→    persistedNumGenerations,
   233→    persistedPrompt,
   234→    editMode,
   235→    inpaintNumGenerations,
   236→    inpaintPrompt,
   237→    setEditMode: (mode) => setEditMode(toInpaintingEditMode(mode)),
   238→    setInpaintNumGenerations,
   239→    setInpaintPrompt,
   240→    setPersistedEditMode: (mode) => setPersistedEditMode(mode),
   241→    setPersistedNumGenerations,
   242→    setPersistedPrompt,
   243→  });
   244→
   245→  const handleExitInpaintMode = useCallback(() => {
   246→    setIsInpaintMode(false);
   247→  }, [setIsInpaintMode]);
   248→
   249→  // ========================================
   250→  // MAGIC EDIT MODE HOOK
   251→  // ========================================
   252→
   253→  const magicEditHook = useMagicEditMode({
   254→    media,
   255→    selectedProjectId,
   256→    isInpaintMode,
   257→    setIsInpaintMode,
   258→    handleEnterInpaintMode,
   259→    handleGenerateInpaint,
   260→    brushStrokes,
   261→    inpaintPrompt,
   262→    setInpaintPrompt,
   263→    inpaintNumGenerations,
   264→    setInpaintNumGenerations,
   265→    editModeLoras: effectiveEditModeLoras,
   266→    sourceUrlForTasks: effectiveImageUrl,
   267→    imageDimensions,
   268→    toolTypeOverride,
   269→    isInSceneBoostEnabled: false,
   270→    setIsInSceneBoostEnabled: () => {},
   271→    activeVariantId: activeVariant?.id,
   272→    activeVariantLocation: activeVariant?.location,
   273→    createAsGeneration,
   274→    advancedSettings,
   275→    qwenEditModel,
   276→    enabled: true,
   277→    initialActive,
   278→  });
   279→
   280→  const {
   281→    isMagicEditMode, isSpecialEditMode,
   282→    handleEnterMagicEditMode, handleExitMagicEditMode, handleUnifiedGenerate,
   283→  } = magicEditHook;
   284→
   285→  // ========================================
   286→  // REPOSITION MODE HOOK
   287→  // ========================================
   288→
   289→  const repositionHook = useRepositionMode({
   290→    media,
   291→    selectedProjectId,
   292→    imageDimensions,
   293→    imageContainerRef,
   294→    loras: effectiveEditModeLoras,
   295→    inpaintPrompt,
   296→    inpaintNumGenerations,
   297→    toolTypeOverride,
   298→    shotId,
   299→    onVariantCreated: setActiveVariantId,
   300→    refetchVariants,
   301→    createAsGeneration,
   302→    advancedSettings,
   303→    activeVariantLocation: activeVariant?.location,
   304→    activeVariantId: activeVariant?.id,
   305→    activeVariantParams: activeVariant?.params as Record<string, unknown> | null,
   306→    qwenEditModel,
   307→  });
   308→
   309→  const { handleGenerateReposition, handleSaveAsVariant } = repositionHook;
   310→
   311→  // ========================================
   312→  // IMG2IMG MODE HOOK
   313→  // ========================================
   314→
   315→  const img2imgHook = useImg2ImgMode({
   316→    media,
   317→    selectedProjectId,
   318→    isVideo: false,
   319→    availableLoras,
   320→    state: {
   321→      strength: persistedImg2imgStrength,
   322→      setStrength: setPersistedImg2imgStrength,
   323→      enablePromptExpansion: persistedImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion,
   324→      setEnablePromptExpansion: setPersistedImg2imgEnablePromptExpansion,
   325→      prompt: persistedImg2imgPrompt,
   326→      setPrompt: setPersistedImg2imgPrompt,
   327→      promptHasBeenSet: persistedImg2imgPromptHasBeenSet,
   328→      numGenerations: persistedNumGenerations,
   329→    },
   330→    source: {
   331→      baseImageUrl: effectiveImageUrl,
   332→      activeVariantLocation: activeVariant?.location,
   333→      activeVariantId: activeVariant?.id,
   334→      shotId,
   335→    },
   336→    options: {
   337→      toolTypeOverride,
   338→      createAsGeneration,
   339→    },
   340→  });
   341→
   342→  const { handleGenerateImg2Img, loraManager: img2imgLoraManager } = img2imgHook;
   343→
   344→  // ========================================
   345→  // BUILD ImageEditContext VALUE
   346→  // ========================================
   347→
   348→  const imageEditValue = useMemo<ImageEditState>(
   349→    () => buildImageEditStateValue({
   350→      inpainting: inpaintingHook,
   351→      magic: magicEditHook,
   352→      reposition: repositionHook,
   353→      img2img: img2imgHook,
   354→      imageContainerRef,
   355→      handleExitInpaintMode,
   356→      setEditMode: setEditMode as ImageEditState['setEditMode'],
   357→      loraMode, setLoraMode,
   358→      customLoraUrl, setCustomLoraUrl,
   359→      createAsGeneration, setCreateAsGeneration,
   360→      qwenEditModel, setQwenEditModel,
   361→      advancedSettings, setAdvancedSettings,
   362→    }),
   363→    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- hook results are objects; deps track leaf values
   364→    [
   365→      inpaintingHook, magicEditHook, repositionHook, img2imgHook,
   366→      imageContainerRef, handleExitInpaintMode, setEditMode,
   367→      loraMode, setLoraMode, customLoraUrl, setCustomLoraUrl,
   368→      createAsGeneration, setCreateAsGeneration, qwenEditModel, setQwenEditModel,
   369→      advancedSettings, setAdvancedSettings,
   370→    ],
   371→  );
   372→
   373→  return {
   374→    imageEditValue,
   375→    isInpaintMode,
   376→    isMagicEditMode,
   377→    isSpecialEditMode,
   378→    editMode,
   379→    handleEnterMagicEditMode,
   380→    handleExitMagicEditMode,
   381→    handleUnifiedGenerate,
   382→    handleGenerateAnnotatedEdit,
   383→    handleGenerateReposition,
   384→    handleSaveAsVariant,
   385→    handleGenerateImg2Img,
   386→    img2imgLoraManager,
   387→  };
   388→}
   389→

Lines 93-114 in auth.ts contain the JWT decoding logic. Let me understand what's being claimed about this. The claim says "decodes without verifying". Let me read those exact lines again carefully:

Looking back at the auth.ts content I read, lines 93-114 are:
```
  // 2) If JWT user auth is enabled, try to decode JWT and extract user ID
  if (options.allowJwtUserAuth) {
    try {
      const parts = token.split(".");
      if (parts.length === 3) {
        const payloadB64 = parts[1];
        const padded = payloadB64 + "=".repeat((4 - payloadB64.length % 4) % 4);
        const payload = JSON.parse(atob(padded));

        // Check if this is a regular user JWT (not service role)
        const role = payload.role || payload.app_metadata?.role;
        if (!["service_role", "supabase_admin"].includes(role) && payload.sub) {
          return {
            isServiceRole: false,
            userId: payload.sub,
            success: true,
            isJwtAuth: true
          };
        }
      }
    } catch {
      // Not a valid JWT - continue to PAT lookup
    }
  }
```

This is indeed **unverified JWT decoding** - no signature verification at all. Anyone can create a JWT with any user_id and submit it.

## Verification Results

I've thoroughly examined the actual codebase and found the step 1 claim is **substantially inaccurate**. Here are the specific findings:

### File Location Issue
- **Claim**: File is at `src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useInlineEditState.ts`
- **Reality**: File is at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/edit-images/hooks/useInlineEditState.ts`
- The file does not exist in the MediaLightbox directory at all.

### Line Count - Partially Accurate
- **Claim**: 468 lines
- **Reality**: Exactly 468 lines ✓ (accurate)

### Hook Count - Inaccurate
- **Claim**: "manually reshapes ~10 hook returns"
- **Reality**: Calls/uses these hooks:
  1. `useInlineEditEnvironment` (internal helper)
  2. `useInlineEditPersistence` (internal helper)
  3. `useInlineEditInpaintingAndMagic` (internal helper)
  4. `useInlineEditReposition` (internal helper)
  5. `useInlineEditImg2Img` (internal helper)
  6. `useInlineEditSettingsSync` (internal hook)
  7. `usePublicLoras` (called from main hook)
  8. `useSourceGeneration` (called from main hook)
  9. `useStarToggle` (called from main hook)

The file calls **9 hooks**, not "~10". More importantly, 5 of these are **internal helper functions** that organize and encapsulate behavior, not just forwarding.

### Behavioral Contribution - The Claim is **Wrong**
The "zero behavioral contribution" claim is **inaccurate**. The hook contains real behavior:

1. **`resolveActualGenerationId()`** (lines 48–52): Complex logic resolving shot generation IDs with nullability handling
2. **`toInpaintingEditMode()`** (lines 40–47): Type conversion with fallback logic
3. **`useInlineEditEnvironment()`** (lines 53–90): Manages 6 refs, 2 pieces of state, resolves cloud mode, upscale state, and more
4. **`useInlineEditPersistence()`** (lines 92–102): Coordinates two persistence hooks
5. **`useInlineEditInpaintingAndMagic()`** (lines 104–154): Wires inpainting and magic edit with **circular ref handling** (lines 150–152) for exit mode coordination
6. **`useInlineEditReposition()`** (lines 156–177): Wires reposition with variant callbacks
7. **`useInlineEditImg2Img()`** (lines 179–209): Shapes img2img params from persistence
8. **`useInlineEditSettingsSync()`** (lines 211–232): Syncs edit mode with type conversion
9. **`buildInlineEditStateModels()`** (lines 244–320): Builds three nested state objects (inpaintingState, transformState, generationState) with hand-picked selections and grouping by concern

### Comparison to Lightbox Orchestrator
There's a parallel hook `useImageEditOrchestrator` in the lightbox (388 lines). Both are similar:
- Both wire 4 major edit mode hooks
- Both use the shared factory `buildImageEditStateValue` 
- Inline version has 80 more lines because it **additionally**:
  - Manages its own environment (refs, state, upscale)
  - Handles variant coordination with `activeVariant` logic
  - Manages upscale state coordination

### Consumer Pattern
- **Single consumer**: `InlineEditView.tsx` (the inline editor)
- Inlining would require moving 468 lines into the consumer component, which currently is ~200 lines
- Would create massive prop drilling through multiple layout/canvas components (MediaDisplayWithCanvas, TopRightControls, etc.)

### Verdict
The step's claim of "zero behavioral contribution" is **objectively false**. The hook contains:
- Two type conversion/logic helpers
- Five internal wiring helpers that encapsulate hook coordination
- One builder function that groups ~30 fields into semantic concerns
- Real circular dependency handling for inpaint mode exit
- Variant coordination logic

**Would inlining help?** Probably not. The hook serves to keep a single consumer component under 300 LOC by separating orchestration from layout concerns. Inlining would harm readability without code reduction (it would increase the consumer's complexity).

**Recommendation**: Mark this item as a false positive. The clustering algorithm appears to have mischaracterized this as "shape-shifting" when it's actually **proper abstraction** of edit mode orchestration. The file is well-factored for its purpose.

## Verification Report: Contract-Dedup Cluster Step 1

### Summary

The step contains **significant inaccuracies**. Here's what I found:

---

### 1. **Files Exist: TRUE**
Both files exist:
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/taskParamsUtils.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/TasksPane/utils/task-utils.ts`

### 2. **Number of Functions: CLAIM IS WRONG**

The step claims there are "two competing deriveInputImages functions." This is **inaccurate**. There are actually **THREE separate implementations**:

1. **`deriveInputImages`** in `/src/shared/lib/taskParamsUtils.ts` (lines 36-95) - exported function
2. **`deriveTaskInputImages`** in `/src/shared/components/TasksPane/utils/task-utils.ts` (lines 37-80) - exported function
3. **`deriveInputImages`** in `/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useAdjustedTaskDetails.ts` (lines 21-48) - private helper function

The claim conflates the two main functions by using the wrong name for the TasksPane version. It's called `deriveTaskInputImages`, not `deriveInputImages`.

### 3. **Actual Differences Between Functions**

The three implementations have **fundamentally different designs**, not just "divergent field-priority contracts":

| Aspect | `taskParamsUtils.ts` | `TasksPane/task-utils.ts` | `MediaLightbox` |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| **Export** | Yes (canonical) | Yes | No (private) |
| **Signature** | `deriveInputImages(parsedParams: Record<string, unknown>): string[]` | `deriveTaskInputImages(task: Task \| null): string[]` | `deriveInputImages(params: Record<string, unknown>): string[]` |
| **Input** | Parsed params object | Task object | Params object |
| **Travel Task Handling** | Has dedicated `deriveTravelInputImages` with source ordering | No travel-specific logic | No travel logic |
| **Segment Task Logic** | Complex: segment-only images first, then fallback chain | Simple: only checks `individual_travel_segment` taskType | No segment-specific logic |
| **Fields Checked** | 8+ single fields + arrays + orchestrator + travel reader | 6 single fields + arrays + orchestrator | 2 main arrays + start/end URLs + orchestrator |
| **Deduplication** | `Array.from(new Set())` | No deduplication | `[...new Set()]` |

### 4. **Key Contract Differences**

**taskParamsUtils.ts** (most complete):
- Priority for segments: `individual_segment_params.input_image_paths_resolved` → `start/end_image_url` → top-level fallback
- Checks: `image_url`, `image`, `input_image`, `init_image`, `control_image`, `images[]`, `input_images[]`, `mask_url`
- Has **travel-specific source ordering logic** with `TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER` / `TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER`
- Deduplicates results

**TasksPane/task-utils.ts** (simpler):
- Only checks: `input_image`, `image`, `init_image`, `control_image`, `images[]`, `input_images[]`
- Segment handling: only checks `taskType === 'individual_travel_segment'`
- No deduplication
- **Missing**: `mask_url`, travel task detection, travel source ordering, segment image fallback chain

**MediaLightbox** (minimal, unused):
- Private helper in hook
- Only checks: `input_images[]`, orchestrator `input_images[]`, start/end URLs
- **Missing**: Most single-field checks, segment logic, travel detection

### 5. **Caller Distribution**

**`deriveInputImages` (taskParamsUtils.ts):** 7 call sites
- `normalizeTaskDetailsPayload.ts` (1)
- `useVideoTravelTaskData.ts` (1)
- `useGenerationTaskDetails.ts` (1)
- `useGenerationDetails.ts` (1)
- Test file (3+ calls)

**`deriveTaskInputImages` (TasksPane/task-utils.ts):** 2 call sites
- `useTasksLightbox.ts` (1)
- Test file (12+ calls)

**`deriveInputImages` (MediaLightbox):** 1 call site
- Internal to `useAdjustedTaskDetails.ts` (1 local use)

### 6. **Merge Strategy Assessment**

**The proposed merge strategy (keep taskParamsUtils.ts as canonical) is SENSIBLE, but incomplete:**

**Correct reasoning:**
- taskParamsUtils.ts has more comprehensive logic (travel detection, segment fallback chains, source ordering)
- It's already used in TaskDetails and GenerationDetails
- It has proper deduplication

**Missing consideration:**
- TasksPane's `deriveTaskInputImages` takes a `Task` object, not parsed params
- It filters out empty strings from arrays (line 23), while taskParamsUtils doesn't
- The merge would need an adapter pattern OR the TasksPane caller would need to parse params first

**What's actually wrong:**
- The merge can't be a simple "delete one, keep the other" — they have different input signatures
- MediaLightbox's private implementation can definitely be removed (it's unused externally)
- The deduplication approach differs (Set vs no dedup in TasksPane)

---

### Conclusion

**Accuracy of the step: 30%**
- Correctly identifies two functions exist ✓
- Incorrectly names the second function ✗
- Misses a third implementation entirely ✗
- Correctly identifies they should be deduplicated ✓
- Correctly identifies taskParamsUtils as canonical ✓
- Oversimplifies the contracts (not just field-priority, but fundamental design differences) ✗
- Doesn't account for signature incompatibility (Task vs parsed params) ✗

## Verification Report: Security-Auth-Fixes Cluster

Based on a thorough inspection of the actual Reigh codebase at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh`, here are my findings:

### **CLAIM 1: JWT decode without verification in supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts (lines 93-114)**

**STATUS: ACCURATE WITH CRITICAL DETAIL**

The file exists at the correct path and lines 93-114 contain the JWT handling code. **However, the security issue is more nuanced than stated:**

**What's actually happening:**
- Lines 93-114 decode JWTs without signature verification (VULNERABLE)
- The code base64-decodes the JWT payload and JSON-parses it without ever checking the JWT signature
- It does include a check to reject JWTs with `service_role` claims (lines 102-103), which prevents a specific escalation
- **But this is NOT sufficient protection** — an attacker can still:
  1. Create a forged JWT with any `user_id` in `payload.sub`
  2. Use it to impersonate that user for any endpoint with `allowJwtUserAuth: true`

**The comment on lines 41-43 is misleading:**
```typescript
// NOTE: We intentionally do NOT accept JWTs with service_role claims.
// This prevents unsigned/forged JWTs from gaining elevated privileges.
```
This comment suggests forged JWTs are blocked, but that's only true for service_role claims. Regular user JWTs are completely unverified.

---

### **CLAIM 2: "15 functions use allowJwtUserAuth: true"**

**STATUS: INACCURATE - SHOULD BE 12, NOT 15**

**Actual count:** 12 functions use `allowJwtUserAuth: true`

Functions that use it:
1. ai-prompt
2. ai-voice-prompt
3. create-task
4. delete-project
5. generate-pat
6. grant-credits
7. huggingface-upload
8. revoke-pat
9. setup-auto-topup
10. stripe-checkout
11. tasks-list
12. trim-video

All 12 of these use `authenticateRequest` directly (not via the safer `withEdgeRequest` wrapper).

---

### **CLAIM 3: "18 functions use raw authenticateRequest() instead of withEdgeRequest wrapper"**

**STATUS: ACCURATE - 18 CONFIRMED**

**Total edge functions:** 31

**Breakdown by authentication pattern:**
- **authenticateRequest (direct):** 18 functions — these call `authenticateRequest()` directly inline and handle responses manually
- **withEdgeRequest (wrapper):** 6 functions — these use the safer abstraction layer
- **bootstrapEdgeHandler (direct):** 7 functions — these use the lower-level bootstrap function directly

**The 18 direct authenticateRequest functions are:**
1. ai-prompt ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
2. ai-voice-prompt ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
3. broadcast-realtime
4. calculate-task-cost
5. create-task ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
6. delete-project ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
7. discord-daily-stats
8. generate-thumbnail
9. get-predecessor-output
10. grant-credits ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
11. huggingface-upload ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
12. stripe-webhook
13. task-counts
14. tasks-list ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
15. trigger-auto-topup
16. trim-video ✓ uses allowJwtUserAuth
17. update-task-status
18. update-worker-model

---

### **Summary of Accuracy**

| Claim | Status | Details |
|-------|--------|---------|
| Auth file location & JWT decode issue | ACCURATE | File exists, JWT decode without verification confirmed |
| 15 functions use allowJwtUserAuth | **WRONG - SHOULD BE 12** | Off by 3 |
| 18 functions use raw authenticateRequest | **ACCURATE** | Confirmed exact count |

### **The Real Security Issue**

The vulnerability is real but the cluster statement is incomplete. The danger is:
- 12 functions accept unverified JWTs (not 15)
- These 12 are vulnerable to JWT forgery for user impersonation
- 6 functions properly use `withEdgeRequest` which wraps auth handling safely (though none enable allowJwtUserAuth)
- 7 functions use `bootstrapEdgeHandler` directly, which is the underlying safe mechanism

The proper fix would be to either:
1. Remove `allowJwtUserAuth` support entirely, OR
2. Implement proper JWT signature verification before trusting `payload.sub`, OR
3. Use `withEdgeRequest` for all authenticated endpoints to ensure consistency

   390→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   391→) -> None:
   392→    """Record the ENRICH stage: validate steps have detail/refs for executor readiness.
   393→
   394→    This stage sits between organize and commit. It checks whether action steps
   395→    are detailed enough for an executor with zero context. Steps should have
   396→    ``detail`` (sub-points) and/or ``issue_refs`` (for auto-completion).
   397→
   398→    The agent can still go back and organize (add/remove clusters, reorder)
   399→    at this point — the stage just validates step quality.
   400→    """
   401→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   402→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   403→
   404→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   405→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   406→
   407→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   408→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to enrich.", "yellow"))
   409→        return
   410→
   411→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   412→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   413→
   414→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   415→    existing_stage = stages.get("enrich")
   416→    report, is_reuse = _resolve_reusable_report(report, existing_stage)
   417→
   418→    if not _require_organize_stage_for_enrich(stages):
   419→        return
   420→
   421→    # Auto-confirm organize if attestation provided
   422→    if not stages.get("organize", {}).get("confirmed_at"):
   423→        if attestation:
   424→            from ._stage_validation import _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete
   425→            if not _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete(
   426→                plan=plan, stages=stages, attestation=attestation,
   427→            ):
   428→                return
   429→        else:
   430→            print(colorize("  Cannot enrich: organize stage not confirmed.", "red"))
   431→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify plan triage --confirm organize", "dim"))
   432→            print(colorize("  Or pass --attestation to auto-confirm organize inline.", "dim"))
   433→            return
   434→
   435→    # Check shallow steps — block if any steps lack detail or issue_refs
   436→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   437→    total_bare = sum(n for _, n, _ in shallow)
   438→
   439→    if shallow:
   440→        print(colorize(f"  Cannot enrich: {total_bare} step(s) across {len(shallow)} cluster(s) lack detail or issue_refs:", "red"))
   441→        for name, bare, total in shallow:
   442→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps need enrichment", "yellow"))
   443→        print()
   444→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --detail (sub-points) or --issue-refs (for auto-completion).", "dim"))
   445→        print(colorize("  Fix:", "dim"))
   446→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   447→        print(colorize("  You can also still reorganize: add/remove clusters, reorder, etc.", "dim"))
   448→        return
   449→    else:
   450→        print(colorize("  All steps have detail or issue_refs.", "green"))
   451→
   452→    report = _enrich_report_or_error(report)
   453→    if report is None:
   454→        return
   455→
   456→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   457→    cleared = _record_enrich_stage(
   458→        stages,
   459→        report=report,
   460→        shallow_count=total_bare,
   461→        existing_stage=existing_stage,
   462→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   463→    )
   464→
   465→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   466→
   467→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   468→        plan,
   469→        "triage_enrich",
   470→        actor="user",
   471→        detail={"shallow_count": total_bare, "reuse": is_reuse},
   472→    )
   473→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   474→
   475→    print(colorize(
   476→        f"  Enrich stage recorded: {total_bare} step(s) still without detail.",
   477→        "green",
   478→    ))
   479→    if is_reuse:
   480→        print(colorize("  Enrich data preserved (no changes).", "dim"))
   481→        if cleared:
   482→            print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared, stages)
   483→    else:
   484→        print(colorize("  Now confirm the enrichment.", "yellow"))
   485→        print(colorize("    desloppify plan triage --confirm enrich", "dim"))
   486→
   487→    print_user_message(
   488→        "Hey — enrich is recorded. Before confirming, double-check"
   489→        " that every step is clear enough for an executor with zero"
   490→        " context. Add --detail to any step that's too vague. You"
   491→        " can still reorganize at this point (add/remove clusters,"
   492→        " reorder items). Once satisfied, confirm and complete triage."
   493→    )

   232→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:

   234→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   235→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():

   238→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   239→        if not steps:

   241→        bare = sum(
   242→            1 for s in steps
   243→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   244→        )
   245→        if bare > 0:
   246→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   247→    return results

   415→def _completion_clusters_valid(plan: dict, state: dict | None = None) -> bool:

   445→        return False

   447→    # Check for unclustered review issues

   449→    if unclustered:

   451→        for fid in unclustered[:5]:

   586→def _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note: str, si) -> bool:
   587→    new_ids = si.new_since_last
   588→    if not new_ids:
   589→        return True
   590→    valid_ids = set(si.open_issues.keys())
   591→    cited = extract_issue_citations(note, valid_ids)
   592→    new_cited = cited & new_ids
   593→    if new_cited:
   594→        return True
   595→    print(colorize("  Note must cite at least 1 new/changed issue.", "red"))
   596→    print(colorize(f"  {len(new_ids)} new issue(s) since last triage:", "dim"))
   597→    for fid in sorted(new_ids)[:5]:
   598→        print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   599→    if len(new_ids) > 5:
   600→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(new_ids) - 5} more", "dim"))
   601→    return False

   427→def _cmd_confirm_stage(
   428→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   429→    *,
   430→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   431→) -> None:
   432→    """Router for ``--confirm observe/reflect/organize/enrich``."""
   433→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   434→    confirm_stage = getattr(args, "confirm", None)
   435→    attestation = getattr(args, "attestation", None)

   437→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})

   439→
   440→    if confirm_stage == "observe":

   442→    elif confirm_stage == "reflect":

   444→    elif confirm_stage == "organize":
   445→        _confirm_organize(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   446→    elif confirm_stage == "enrich":
   447→        _confirm_enrich(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   448→
   449→
   450→MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN = _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN
   451→validate_attestation = _validate_attestation
   452→

    37→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    38→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    39→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    40→    if plan is not None:
    41→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    42→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    43→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    44→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    45→                all_ids.append(fid)
    46→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    47→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    48→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    49→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    50→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    51→
    52→    for pattern in patterns:
    53→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    54→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    55→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    56→
    57→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    58→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    59→            if suggestions:
    60→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    61→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    62→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    63→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    64→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    65→            continue
    66→
    67→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    68→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    69→        for fid in all_ids:
    70→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    71→                suggestions.append(fid)
    72→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    73→                suggestions.append(fid)

    76→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))

   106→        cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, description, action=action)
   107→    except ValueError as ex:
   108→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   109→        return
   110→
   111→    if priority is not None:
   112→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   113→    if steps_file is not None:
   114→        path = Path(steps_file)
   115→        if not path.is_file():
   116→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   117→            return
   118→        steps = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   119→        cluster["action_steps"] = steps
   120→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(steps)} step(s) from {steps_file}", "dim"))
   121→
   122→    append_log_entry(
   123→        plan, "cluster_create", cluster_name=name, actor="user",
   124→        detail={"description": description, "action": action},
   125→    )
   126→    save_plan(plan)
   127→    print(colorize(f"  Created cluster: {name}", "green"))

   130→def _cmd_cluster_add(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   131→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   132→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   133→        return
   134→
   135→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   136→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   137→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   138→
   139→    plan = load_plan()
   140→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   141→    if not issue_ids:
   142→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   143→        _print_pattern_hints()
   144→        _suggest_close_matches(state, plan, patterns)
   145→        return
   146→
   147→    if dry_run:
   148→        print(colorize(f"  [dry-run] Would add {len(issue_ids)} item(s) to {cluster_name}:", "cyan"))
   149→        for fid in issue_ids:
   150→            print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   151→        return
   152→
   153→    try:
   154→        count = add_to_cluster(plan, cluster_name, issue_ids)
   155→    except ValueError as ex:
   156→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   157→        return
   158→
   159→    # Check for overlap with other manual clusters
   160→    member_set = set(issue_ids)
   161→    for other_name, other_cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   162→        if other_name == cluster_name or other_cluster.get("auto"):
   163→            continue
   164→        other_ids = set(other_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   165→        if not other_ids:
   166→            continue
   167→        overlap = member_set & other_ids
   168→        if len(overlap) > len(other_ids) * 0.5:
   169→            print(colorize(
   170→                f"  Warning: {len(overlap)} issue(s) also in cluster '{other_name}' "
   171→                f"({len(overlap)}/{len(other_ids)} = {int(len(overlap)/len(other_ids)*100)}% overlap).",
   172→                "yellow",
   173→            ))
   174→
   175→    append_log_entry(
   176→        plan, "cluster_add", issue_ids=issue_ids, cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   177→    )
   178→    save_plan(plan)
   179→    print(colorize(f"  Added {count} item(s) to cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))

   231→
   232→def _resolve_item_position(
   233→    position: str,
   234→    target: str | None,
   235→    item_ids: list[str],
   236→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   237→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   238→    cluster_name: str,
   239→    state: dict,
   240→    plan: dict,
   241→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   242→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   243→
   244→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   245→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   246→    """
   247→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   248→
   249→    if position == "top":
   250→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   251→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   252→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   253→            return None
   254→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   255→
   256→    if position == "bottom":
   257→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   258→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   259→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   260→            return None
   261→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   262→
   263→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   264→        if target is None:
   265→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   266→            return None
   267→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   268→        if not target_ids:
   269→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   270→            return None
   271→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   272→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   273→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   274→            return None
   275→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   276→
   277→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   278→        if target is None:
   279→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   280→            return None
   281→        try:
   282→            offset = int(target)
   283→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   284→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   285→            return None
   286→        return (position, None, offset)
   287→
   288→    return (position, None, None)
   289→
   290→
   291→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   292→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   293→    plan: dict,
   294→    clusters: dict,
   295→    cluster_names: list[str],
   296→    position: str,
   297→    target: str | None,
   298→    item_pattern: str,
   299→) -> None:
   300→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   301→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   302→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   303→        return
   304→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   305→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   306→
   307→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   308→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   309→    if not item_ids:
   310→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   311→        return
   312→    for fid in item_ids:
   313→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   314→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   315→            return
   316→
   317→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   318→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   319→
   320→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   321→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   322→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   323→    )
   324→    if result is None:
   325→        return
   326→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   327→
   328→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   329→    append_log_entry(
   330→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   331→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   332→    )
   333→    save_plan(plan)
   334→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   335→
   336→
   337→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   338→    plan: dict,
   339→    clusters: dict,
   340→    cluster_names: list[str],
   341→    position: str,
   342→    target: str | None,
   343→) -> None:
   344→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   345→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   346→
   347→    offset = None
   348→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   349→        try:
   350→            offset = int(target)
   351→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   353→            return
   354→        target = None
   355→
   356→    seen: set[str] = set()
   357→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   358→    for name in cluster_names:
   359→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   360→            if fid not in seen:
   361→                seen.add(fid)
   362→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   363→
   364→    if not all_member_ids:
   365→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   369→    append_log_entry(
   370→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   371→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   372→    )
   373→    save_plan(plan)
   374→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   376→
   377→
   378→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   379→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   380→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   381→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   382→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   383→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   384→
   385→    plan = load_plan()
   386→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   387→
   388→    # Validate all names exist
   389→    for name in cluster_names:
   390→        if name not in clusters:
   391→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   392→            return
   393→
   394→    if item_pattern is not None:
   395→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   396→    else:
   397→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)

   421→def _print_step(i: int, step: str | dict) -> None:
   422→    """Print a single step with title, detail, refs, and done status."""
   423→    if isinstance(step, str):
   424→        print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))
   425→        return
   426→    done = step.get("done", False)
   427→    marker = "[x]" if done else "[ ]"
   428→    title = step.get("title", "")
   429→    print(f"    {i}. {marker} {title}")
   430→    if done:
   431→        print(colorize("         (completed)", "dim"))
   432→        return
   433→    detail = step.get("detail", "")
   434→    if detail:
   435→        for line in detail.splitlines():
   436→            print(colorize(f"         {line}", "dim"))
   437→    refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
   438→    if refs:
   439→        print(colorize(f"         Refs: {', '.join(refs)}", "dim"))

   442→def _cmd_cluster_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   443→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   444→    plan = load_plan()

   446→    if cluster is None:

   448→        return
   449→
   450→    # Header
   451→    auto_tag = "Auto-generated" if cluster.get("auto") else "Manual"
   452→    cluster_key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   453→    key_type = f" ({cluster_key.split('::', 1)[0]})" if cluster_key else ""
   454→    print(colorize(f"  Cluster: {cluster_name}", "bold"))
   455→    print(colorize(f"  Type: {auto_tag}{key_type}", "dim"))
   456→    priority = cluster.get("priority")
   457→    if priority is not None:

   459→    dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   460→    if dep_order is not None:
   461→        print(colorize(f"  Dependency order: {dep_order}", "dim"))

   463→    if desc:
   464→        print(colorize(f"  Description: {desc}", "dim"))

   466→    if action:

   470→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   471→    if steps:
   472→        done_count = sum(1 for s in steps if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("done", False))
   473→        print()
   474→        suffix = f" — {done_count}/{len(steps)} done" if done_count else ""
   475→        print(colorize(f"  Steps ({len(steps)}){suffix}:", "dim"))
   476→        for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):

   486→        print(colorize(f"  Members ({len(issue_ids)}):", "dim"))

   490→    # Commands

   494→    print(colorize(f"    Drill in:     desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10", "dim"))
   495→    print(colorize(f"    Skip:         desloppify plan skip {cluster_name}", "dim"))

   497→
   498→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   499→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   500→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   501→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   502→
   503→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   504→    clusters sort by queue position.
   505→
   506→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   507→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   508→    """
   509→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   510→
   511→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   512→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   513→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   514→
   515→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   516→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   517→        clusters.items(),
   518→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   519→    )
   520→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   521→
   522→
   523→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   524→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   525→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   526→    active: str | None,
   527→) -> None:
   528→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   529→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   530→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   531→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)
   532→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   533→    print()
   534→    dep_header = f"  {'Dep':>3}" if has_dep else ""
   535→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Pri':>3}{dep_header}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   536→    dep_sep = f"  {'─'*3}" if has_dep else ""
   537→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*3}{dep_sep}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*40}"
   538→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   539→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   540→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   541→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   542→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   543→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   544→        pri_str = str(priority) if priority is not None else "—"
   545→        dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   546→        dep_str = f"  {dep_order:>3}" if has_dep and dep_order is not None else ("  {:>3}".format("—") if has_dep else "")
   547→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   548→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   549→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   550→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   551→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   552→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   553→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   554→        desc_truncated = (desc[:39] + "…") if len(desc) > 40 else desc
   555→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   556→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   557→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {pri_str:>3}{dep_str}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   558→    print()
   559→
   560→
   561→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   562→    plan = load_plan()
   563→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   564→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   565→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   566→    missing_steps: bool = getattr(args, "missing_steps", False)
   567→
   568→    if not clusters:
   569→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   570→        return
   571→
   572→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   573→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   574→
   575→    if missing_steps:
   576→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.stage_helpers import _unenriched_clusters
   577→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   578→        if not gaps:
   579→            print(colorize("  All clusters have action steps.", "green"))
   580→            return
   581→        print(colorize(f"  {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need action steps:", "bold"))
   582→        for name, missing in gaps:
   583→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   584→        print()
   585→        print(colorize("  Fix with:", "dim"))
   586→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   587→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "step title" --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   588→        return
   589→
   590→    if verbose:
   591→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   592→        return
   593→
   594→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   595→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   596→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   597→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   598→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   599→        pri_tag = f" [P{priority}]" if priority is not None else ""

   608→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   609→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   610→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   611→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   612→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   613→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   614→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   615→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   616→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   617→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   618→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   619→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   620→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   621→
   622→    has_update = any(x is not None for x in [
   623→        description, steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step,
   624→        remove_step, done_step, undone_step, priority,
   625→    ])
   626→    if not has_update:
   627→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description, --steps, --steps-file, --add-step, --priority, etc.", "yellow"))
   628→        return
   629→
   630→    plan = load_plan()
   631→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   632→    if cluster is None:
   633→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   634→        return
   635→
   636→    if description is not None:
   637→        cluster["description"] = description
   638→
   639→    if priority is not None:
   640→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   641→        print(colorize(f"  Priority set to {priority}.", "dim"))
   642→
   643→    # Steps replacement: --steps-file takes precedence over --steps
   644→    if steps_file is not None:
   645→        path = Path(steps_file)
   646→        if not path.is_file():
   647→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   648→            return
   649→        parsed = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   650→        cluster["action_steps"] = parsed
   651→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(parsed)} step(s) from {steps_file}.", "dim"))
   652→    elif steps is not None:
   653→        # Legacy flat strings → wrap as ActionStep dicts
   654→        cluster["action_steps"] = [normalize_step(s) for s in steps]
   655→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s).", "dim"))
   656→
   657→    # Incremental step operations
   658→    current_steps: list = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   659→
   660→    if add_step is not None:
   661→        new_step: dict = {"title": add_step}
   662→        if detail is not None:
   663→            new_step["detail"] = detail
   664→        current_steps.append(new_step)
   665→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   666→        print(colorize(f"  Added step {len(current_steps)}: {add_step}", "dim"))
   667→
   668→    if update_step is not None:
   669→        idx = update_step - 1
   670→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   671→            print(colorize(f"  Step {update_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   672→            return
   673→        old = current_steps[idx]
   674→        if isinstance(old, str):
   675→            old = {"title": old}
   676→        if add_step is None:
   677→            # When --update-step is used without --add-step, keep title, update detail only
   678→            if detail is not None:
   679→                old["detail"] = detail
   680→        else:
   681→            old["title"] = add_step
   682→            if detail is not None:
   683→                old["detail"] = detail
   684→        current_steps[idx] = old
   685→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   686→        print(colorize(f"  Updated step {update_step}.", "dim"))
   687→
   688→    if remove_step is not None:
   689→        idx = remove_step - 1
   690→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   691→            print(colorize(f"  Step {remove_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   692→            return
   693→        removed = current_steps.pop(idx)
   694→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   695→        title = step_summary(removed)
   696→        print(colorize(f"  Removed step {remove_step}: {title}", "dim"))
   697→
   698→    if done_step is not None:
   699→        idx = done_step - 1
   700→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   701→            print(colorize(f"  Step {done_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   702→            return
   703→        step = current_steps[idx]
   704→        if isinstance(step, str):
   705→            step = {"title": step}
   706→            current_steps[idx] = step
   707→        step["done"] = True
   708→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   709→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {done_step} as done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   710→
   711→    if undone_step is not None:
   712→        idx = undone_step - 1
   713→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   714→            print(colorize(f"  Step {undone_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   715→            return
   716→        step = current_steps[idx]
   717→        if isinstance(step, str):
   718→            step = {"title": step}
   719→            current_steps[idx] = step
   720→        step["done"] = False
   721→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   722→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {undone_step} as not done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   723→
   724→    # Show resulting steps after any mutation
   725→    final_steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   726→    if final_steps and any(x is not None for x in [steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step, remove_step, done_step, undone_step]):
   727→        print()
   728→        print(colorize(f"  Current steps ({len(final_steps)}):", "dim"))
   729→        for i, s in enumerate(final_steps, 1):
   730→            _print_step(i, s)
   731→
   732→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   733→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   734→    append_log_entry(
   735→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   736→        detail={"description": description},
   737→    )
   738→    save_plan(plan)
   739→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))
   740→

   742→def _cmd_cluster_export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   743→    """Export cluster steps to stdout in text or YAML format."""
   744→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   745→    export_format: str = getattr(args, "export_format", "text")
   746→
   747→    plan = load_plan()
   748→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   749→    if cluster is None:
   750→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   751→        return
   752→
   753→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   754→    if not steps:
   755→        print(colorize("  No steps to export.", "yellow"))
   756→        return
   757→
   758→    if export_format == "yaml":
   759→        import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   760→        data = {
   761→            "clusters": [{
   762→                "name": cluster_name,
   763→                "description": cluster.get("description") or "",
   764→                **({"priority": cluster["priority"]} if "priority" in cluster else {}),
   765→                "steps": [
   766→                    normalize_step(s) for s in steps
   767→                ],
   768→            }]
   769→        }
   770→        print(yaml.dump(data, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False))

   774→
   775→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   776→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   777→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   778→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   779→
   780→    path = Path(file_path)
   781→    if not path.is_file():
   782→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   783→        return
   784→
   785→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   786→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   787→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   788→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   789→        return
   790→
   791→    entries = data["clusters"]
   792→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   793→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   794→        return
   795→
   796→    plan = load_plan()
   797→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   798→    created = 0
   799→    updated = 0
   800→
   801→    for entry in entries:
   802→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   803→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   804→            continue
   805→        name = entry["name"]
   806→        is_new = name not in clusters
   807→
   808→        if dry_run:
   809→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   810→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   811→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   812→            continue
   813→
   814→        if is_new:
   815→            try:
   816→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   817→            except ValueError as ex:
   818→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   819→                continue
   820→            created += 1
   821→        else:
   822→            cluster = clusters[name]
   823→            updated += 1
   824→
   825→        if "description" in entry:
   826→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   827→        if "priority" in entry:
   828→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   829→        if "steps" in entry:
   830→            imported_steps = []
   831→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   832→                if isinstance(s, str):
   833→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   834→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   835→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   836→                    if "detail" in s:
   837→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   838→                    if "refs" in s:
   839→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   840→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   841→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   842→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   843→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   844→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   845→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   846→
   847→    if dry_run:
   848→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   849→        return
   850→
   851→    save_plan(plan)
   852→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   853→
   854→
   855→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   856→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   857→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   858→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   859→
   860→    plan = load_plan()
   861→    try:
   862→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   863→    except ValueError as ex:
   864→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   865→        return
   866→
   867→    append_log_entry(
   868→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   869→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   870→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   871→    )
   872→    save_plan(plan)
   873→    print(colorize(
   874→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   875→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   876→        "green",
   877→    ))
   878→
   879→
   880→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   881→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   882→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   883→    dispatch = {
   884→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   885→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   886→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   887→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   888→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   889→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   890→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   891→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   892→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   893→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   894→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   895→    }
   896→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   897→    if handler is None:
   898→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)
   899→        return
   900→    handler(args)
   901→
   902→
   903→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_dispatch"]

    16→  const appError = reportError(error, { context, logData, onError });
    17→
    18→  const shouldShowToast = showToast ?? appError.showToast;
    19→  if (shouldShowToast) {
    20→    presentRuntimeError(appError, toastTitle);
    21→  }
    22→
    23→  return appError;
    24→}
    25→
    26→/** Normalize, present, then throw for caller-level control-flow stops. */
    27→export function normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error: unknown, options: RuntimeErrorOptions): never {
    28→  throw normalizeAndPresentError(error, options);
    29→}

    37→function resolveEffectiveAspectRatio(
    38→  projectAspectRatio: string,
    39→  positionedImages: Array<{ metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null }>,
    40→): string {
    41→  if (positionedImages.length === 0) {
    42→    return projectAspectRatio;
    43→  }
    44→
    45→  const firstImage = positionedImages[0];
    46→  const metadata = firstImage.metadata || {};
    47→  const width = typeof metadata.width === 'number' ? metadata.width : null;
    48→  const height = typeof metadata.height === 'number' ? metadata.height : null;
    49→  if (!width || !height) {
    50→    return projectAspectRatio;
    51→  }
    52→
    53→  return findClosestAspectRatio(width / height);
    54→}

    19→interface AdjacentPreloadContext {

    43→
    44→function extractLoadedImageIds(data: unknown): Array<{ id: string }> {
    45→  if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') {
    46→    return [];
    47→  }
    48→
    49→  const maybeItems = (data as { items?: unknown }).items;
    50→  if (!Array.isArray(maybeItems)) {
    51→    return [];
    52→  }
    53→
    54→  return maybeItems
    55→    .map((item) => {
    56→      if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') {
    57→        return null;
    58→      }
    59→      const id = (item as { id?: unknown }).id;
    60→      return typeof id === 'string' ? { id } : null;
    61→    })
    62→    .filter((item): item is { id: string } => item !== null);
    63→}
    64→
    65→export function cleanupDistantGenerationPages(
    66→  queryClient: QueryClient,
    67→  projectId: string,
    68→  currentPage: number,
    69→  keepRange: number = 2,
    70→): void {
    71→  const allQueries = queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll();
    72→
    73→  allQueries.forEach((query) => {
    74→    const key = query.queryKey;
    75→    if (!Array.isArray(key)) return;
    76→
    77→    if (!isUnifiedProjectGenerationsKey(key, projectId)) {
    78→      return;
    79→    }
    80→
    81→    const page = extractUnifiedProjectGenerationsPage(key, projectId);
    82→    if (page !== null && Math.abs(page - currentPage) > keepRange) {
    83→      const loadedImageIds = extractLoadedImageIds(query.state?.data);
    84→      if (loadedImageIds.length > 0) {
    85→        clearLoadedImages(loadedImageIds);
    86→      }
    87→      queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: query.queryKey });
    88→    }
    89→  });
    90→}
    91→
    92→export function scheduleAdjacentGenerationPagePreload({
    93→  queryClient,
    94→  projectId,
    95→  currentPage,
    96→  totalPages,
    97→  hasMorePages,
    98→  itemsPerPage,
    99→  filters,
   100→  filtersString,
   101→  keepRange = 2,
   102→}: ScheduleAdjacentGenerationPagePreloadOptions): () => void {
   103→  const config = preloadingService.getConfig();
   104→
   105→  const timer = setTimeout(async () => {
   106→    await prefetchAdjacentGenerationPages({
   107→      queryClient,
   108→      projectId,
   109→      currentPage,
   110→      totalPages,
   111→      hasMorePages,
   112→      itemsPerPage,
   113→      filters,
   114→      filtersString,
   115→      keepRange,
   116→      onError: (context, error, logData) => {
   117→        normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
   118→          context,
   119→          showToast: false,
   120→          logData,
   121→        });
   122→      },
   123→    });
   124→  }, config.debounceMs);
   125→
   126→  return () => {
   127→    clearTimeout(timer);
   128→  };
   129→}
   130→
   131→async function prefetchPage(
   132→  context: AdjacentPreloadContext,
   133→  page: number,
   134→  priority: number,
   135→  errorContext: string,
   136→): Promise<void> {
   137→  const {
   138→    queryClient,
   139→    projectId,
   140→    itemsPerPage,
   141→    filters,
   142→    filtersString,
   143→    onError,
   144→  } = context;
   145→
   146→  try {
   147→    await queryClient.prefetchQuery({
   148→      [REDACTED](
   149→        projectId,
   150→        page,
   151→        itemsPerPage,
   152→        filtersString,
   153→      ),
   154→      queryFn: () =>
   155→        fetchGenerations(
   156→          projectId,
   157→          itemsPerPage,
   158→          (page - 1) * itemsPerPage,
   159→          filters,
   160→        ),
   161→      staleTime: 30_000,
   162→    });
   163→
   164→    const cached = queryClient.getQueryData<PaginatedResponse>(
   165→      unifiedGenerationQueryKeys.byProject(projectId, page, itemsPerPage, filtersString),
   166→    );
   167→    if (cached?.items) {
   168→      preloadingService.preloadImages(cached.items, priority);
   169→    }
   170→  } catch (error) {
   171→    onError(errorContext, error, { projectId, page });
   172→  }
   173→}
   174→
   175→export async function prefetchAdjacentGenerationPages(context: AdjacentPreloadContext): Promise<void> {
   176→  const {
   177→    currentPage,
   178→    totalPages,
   179→    hasMorePages,
   180→    keepRange = 2,
   181→  } = context;
   182→
   183→  const hasPrevPage = currentPage > 1;
   184→  const hasNextPage = totalPages === null
   185→    ? hasMorePages
   186→    : currentPage < totalPages;
   187→
   188→  if (hasNextPage) {
   189→    await prefetchPage(context, currentPage + 1, PRIORITY_VALUES.high, 'useAdjacentPagePreloader.prefetchNext');
   190→  }
   191→
   192→  if (hasPrevPage) {
   193→    await prefetchPage(context, currentPage - 1, PRIORITY_VALUES.normal, 'useAdjacentPagePreloader.prefetchPrevious');
   194→  }
   195→
   196→  cleanupDistantGenerationPages(context.queryClient, context.projectId, context.currentPage, keepRange);
   197→}

   106→export function useEditSettingsPersistence({
   107→  generationId,
   108→  projectId,
   109→  enabled = true,
   110→}: UseEditSettingsPersistenceProps): UseEditSettingsPersistenceReturn {
   111→  // Per-generation settings

   122→

   124→  const hasInitializedRef = useRef(false);
   125→  const lastGenerationIdRef = useRef<string | null>(null);
   126→  const [isReady, setIsReady] = useState(false);
   127→

   129→  useEffect(() => {

   131→      hasInitializedRef.current = false;
   132→      lastGenerationIdRef.current = generationId;
   133→      setIsReady(false);
   134→    }
   135→  }, [generationId]);
   136→
   137→  // Extract stable references for the initialization effect
   138→  const { isLoading: genIsLoading, hasPersistedSettings, initializeFromLastUsed } = generationSettings;
   139→  const { lastUsed } = lastUsedSettings;
   140→
   141→  // Initialize from "last used" when generation loads without persisted settings
   142→  useEffect(() => {
   143→    if (!genIsLoading && !hasInitializedRef.current && !hasPersistedSettings && generationId) {
   144→      hasInitializedRef.current = true;
   145→      // Apply "last used" settings (without prompt)
   146→      initializeFromLastUsed(lastUsed);
   147→      setIsReady(true);
   148→    } else if (!genIsLoading && !hasInitializedRef.current && hasPersistedSettings) {
   149→      hasInitializedRef.current = true;
   150→      setIsReady(true);
   151→    }
   152→  }, [generationId, genIsLoading, hasPersistedSettings, initializeFromLastUsed, lastUsed]);
   153→
   154→  // Compute effective values

   156→  // Other settings like prompt, loraMode are per-generation
   157→  const effectiveSettings = useMemo(() => {
   158→    if (generationSettings.isLoading) {
   159→      // Still loading, use defaults but editMode from lastUsed
   160→      return {
   161→        ...DEFAULT_EDIT_SETTINGS,
   162→        editMode: lastUsedSettings.lastUsed.editMode,
   163→      };
   164→    }
   165→
   166→    if (generationSettings.hasPersistedSettings) {

   169→        ...generationSettings.settings,

   172→    }
   173→

   176→    // After initialization, always prefer the live generationSettings state so controls

   193→      };

   197→    return {

   201→  }, [
