   236→  // Show/hide tap-to-place hint when endpoint selection changes
   237→  useEffect(() => {
   238→    if (selectedEndpoint && enabled) {
   239→      tapToPlaceHint.show();
   240→    } else {
   241→      tapToPlaceHint.hide();
   242→    }
   243→  }, [selectedEndpoint, enabled, tapToPlaceHint]);
   244→
   245→  // iPad: touch outside to deselect endpoint
   246→  useClickOutside(
   247→    () => setSelectedEndpoint(null),
   248→    { events: ['touchstart'], enabled: !!selectedEndpoint && !!enabled, delay: 100 },
   249→    outerContainerRef as React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>
   250→  );
   251→
   252→  /** Clear endpoint selection (for use by parent click-outside handlers) */
   253→  const clearSelection = useCallback(() => {
   254→    setSelectedEndpoint(null);
   255→  }, []);
   256→
   257→  // Touch start handler for resize handle endpoints
   258→  const handleEndpointTouchStart = useCallback((_endpoint: 'left' | 'right', e: React.TouchEvent) => {
   259→    if (!enabled) return;
   260→    const touch = e.touches[0];
   261→    touchStartPosRef.current = { x: touch.clientX, y: touch.clientY };
   262→  }, [enabled]);
   263→
   264→  // Touch end handler for resize handle endpoints
   265→  const handleEndpointTouchEnd = useCallback((_endpoint: 'left' | 'right', e: React.TouchEvent) => {
   266→    if (!enabled || !touchStartPosRef.current) return;
   267→
   268→    const touch = e.changedTouches[0];
   269→    const deltaX = Math.abs(touch.clientX - touchStartPosRef.current.x);
   270→    const deltaY = Math.abs(touch.clientY - touchStartPosRef.current.y);
   271→    touchStartPosRef.current = null;
   272→
   273→    if (deltaX > SCROLL_THRESHOLD || deltaY > SCROLL_THRESHOLD) return;
   274→
   275→    e.preventDefault();
   276→    e.stopPropagation();
   277→    setSelectedEndpoint(prev => prev === _endpoint ? null : _endpoint);
   278→  }, [enabled]);
   279→
   280→  const handleStripTapToPlace = useStripTapToPlace({
   281→    enabled,
   282→    selectedEndpoint,
   283→    outerContainerRef,
   284→    onRangeChange,
   285→    stripLeftPercent,
   286→    stripWidthPercent,
   287→    fullMin,
   288→    fullMax,
   289→    fullRange,
   290→    effectiveOutputStart,
   291→    effectiveOutputEnd,
   292→    siblingRanges,
   293→    setSelectedEndpoint,
   294→  });
   295→
   296→  // Track touch start for tap detection on strip body
   297→  const handleStripTouchStart = useCallback((e: React.TouchEvent) => {
   298→    if (!enabled) return;
   299→    const touch = e.touches[0];
   300→    touchStartPosRef.current = { x: touch.clientX, y: touch.clientY };
   301→  }, [enabled]);
   302→
   303→  // Touch end handler for strip body - dispatches to tap-to-place, double-tap, or single-tap
   304→  const handleStripTouchEnd = useCallback((e: React.TouchEvent) => {
   305→    if (!touchStartPosRef.current) return;
   306→
   307→    const touch = e.changedTouches[0];
   308→    const deltaX = Math.abs(touch.clientX - touchStartPosRef.current.x);
   309→    const deltaY = Math.abs(touch.clientY - touchStartPosRef.current.y);
   310→    touchStartPosRef.current = null;
   311→
   312→    if (deltaX > SCROLL_THRESHOLD || deltaY > SCROLL_THRESHOLD) return;
   313→
   314→    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
   315→    if (target.closest('button') || target.closest('[data-resize-handle]')) return;
   316→
   317→    // If endpoint selected and strip active, place it
   318→    if (selectedEndpoint && isStripActive && enabled) {
   319→      handleStripTapToPlace(e);
   320→      return;
   321→    }
   322→
   323→    // Double-tap detection for iPad
   324→    const now = Date.now();
   325→    const timeSinceLastTap = now - lastTapTimeRef.current;
   326→    lastTapTimeRef.current = now;
   327→
   328→    if (timeSinceLastTap < DOUBLE_TAP_DELAY && isTablet) {
   329→      e.preventDefault();
   330→      setSelectedEndpoint(null);
   331→      onDoubleTap();
   332→    } else if (isTablet && !isStripActive) {
   333→      // Single tap - delegate to parent for frame preview
   334→      e.preventDefault();
   335→      onSingleTap(touch as unknown as Touch);
   336→    }
   337→  }, [enabled, selectedEndpoint, handleStripTapToPlace, isTablet, isStripActive, onDoubleTap, onSingleTap]);
   338→
   339→  return {
   340→    selectedEndpoint,
   341→    clearSelection,
   342→    tapToPlaceHintVisible: tapToPlaceHint.isVisible,
   343→    handleEndpointTouchStart,
   344→    handleEndpointTouchEnd,
   345→    handleStripTouchStart,
   346→    handleStripTouchEnd,
   347→  };
   348→}
   349→
   350→/** Returned clearSelection function type for parent click-outside handlers */
   351→export type { UseTabletEndpointSelectionReturn };
   352→

    73→  normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(

   166→async function createGeneration(params: {
   167→  imageUrl: string;
   168→  fileName: string;
   169→  fileType: string;
   170→  fileSize: number;
   171→  projectId: string;
   172→  prompt: string;

   174→  /** Resolution in "WIDTHxHEIGHT" format (e.g., "1920x1080") */
   175→  resolution?: string;

   178→}): Promise<GenerationRow> {

   183→    file_type: params.fileType,
   184→    file_size: params.fileSize,
   185→  };
   186→
   187→  // Add dimension params if provided
   188→  if (params.resolution) {
   189→    generationParams.resolution = params.resolution;
   190→  }
   191→  if (params.aspectRatio) {
   192→    generationParams.aspect_ratio = params.aspectRatio;
   193→  }
   194→
   195→  const { data, error } = await createGenerationRecord({
   196→    imageUrl: params.imageUrl,
   197→    thumbnailUrl: params.thumbnailUrl || params.imageUrl,
   198→    fileType: params.fileType || 'image',
   199→    projectId: params.projectId,
   200→    generationParams,
   201→  });
   202→
   203→  if (error || !data) {
   204→    normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error ?? new Error('Failed to create generation'), {
   205→      context: 'useCreateGeneration.createGeneration',
   206→      showToast: false,
   207→      logData: { projectId: params.projectId },
   208→    });
   209→  }
   210→
   211→  // Create the original variant for this generation
   212→  const { error: variantError } = await createGenerationPrimaryVariant({
   213→    generationId: data.id,
   214→    imageUrl: params.imageUrl,
   215→    thumbnailUrl: params.thumbnailUrl || params.imageUrl,
   216→    generationParams,
   217→    variantType: VARIANT_TYPE.ORIGINAL,
   218→  });
   219→
   220→  if (variantError) {
   221→    normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(variantError, {
   222→      context: 'useCreateGeneration.createVariant',
   223→      showToast: false,
   224→    });
   225→  }
   226→
   227→  return data;
   228→}

   277→function useDeleteFromTable(table: 'generations' | 'generation_variants', entityLabel: string) {
   278→  return useMutation({
   279→    mutationFn: async (input: ScopedGenerationInput | ScopedVariantInput) => {
   280→      const projectId = ensureProjectScope(
   281→        input.projectId,
   282→        `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.projectScope`,
   283→      );
   284→
   285→      if (table === 'generations') {
   286→        await verifyGenerationScope(
   287→          input.id,
   288→          projectId,
   289→          `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.scopeValidation`,
   290→        );
   291→
   292→        const { data, error } = await deleteGenerationByScope({
   293→          id: input.id,
   294→          projectId,
   295→        });
   296→
   297→        if (error) {
   298→          normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error, {
   299→            context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}`,
   300→            showToast: false,
   301→            logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel },
   302→          });
   303→        }
   304→
   305→        if (!data || data.length === 0) {
   306→          normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(new Error('No rows deleted while enforcing generation scope'), {
   307→            context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.noRows`,
   308→            showToast: false,
   309→            logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel },
   310→          });
   311→        }
   312→
   313→        return;
   314→      }
   315→
   316→      const variantScope = await verifyVariantScope(
   317→        input.id,
   318→        projectId,
   319→        `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.scopeValidation`,
   320→      );
   321→      const { data, error } = await deleteGenerationVariantByScope({
   322→        id: input.id,
   323→        generationId: variantScope.generationId,
   324→      });
   325→
   326→      if (error) {
   327→        normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error, {
   328→          context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}`,
   329→          showToast: false,
   330→          logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel, generationId: variantScope.generationId },
   331→        });
   332→      }
   333→
   334→      if (!data || data.length === 0) {
   335→        normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(new Error('No rows deleted while enforcing variant scope'), {
   336→          context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.noRows`,
   337→          showToast: false,
   338→          logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel, generationId: variantScope.generationId },
   339→        });
   340→      }
   341→    },
   342→    onError: (error: Error) => {
   343→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
   344→        context: `useDelete${entityLabel.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + entityLabel.slice(1)}`,
   345→        toastTitle: `Failed to delete ${entityLabel}`,
   346→      });
   347→    },
   348→  });
   349→}

   384→  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
   385→
   386→  return useMutation({
   387→    mutationFn: ({ id, starred, projectId }: { id: string; starred: boolean; projectId: string; shotId?: string }) => {
   388→      return toggleGenerationStar({ id, starred, projectId });
   389→    },
   390→    onMutate: async ({ id, starred, shotId }) => {
   391→      return applyOptimisticGenerationStarUpdate(queryClient, {
   392→        generationId: id,
   393→        starred,
   394→        shotId,
   395→      });
   396→    },
   397→    onError: (error: Error, _variables, context) => {
   398→      rollbackOptimisticGenerationStarUpdate(queryClient, context);
   399→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useToggleGenerationStar', toastTitle: 'Failed to toggle star' });
   400→    },
   401→    onSuccess: (_data, variables) => {
   402→      // Emit custom event so Timeline knows to refetch star data
   403→      if (variables.shotId) {
   404→        dispatchAppEvent('generation-star-updated', {
   405→          generationId: variables.id, shotId: variables.shotId!, starred: variables.starred,
   406→        });

    30→  const controller = new AbortController();
    31→  const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
    32→    controller.abort();
    33→  }, timeoutMs);
    34→
    35→  try {
    36→    // Generate an idempotency key to prevent duplicate task creation from
    37→    // network retries or double-clicks. The server will return the existing

    50→        task_type: taskParams.task_type,
    51→        project_id: taskParams.project_id,
    52→        dependant_on: null,
    53→        idempotency_key,
    54→      }),
    55→      signal: controller.signal,
    56→    });

    25→function parsePendingJoinClips(raw: string): PendingJoinClipParseResult | null {

   102→async function toPendingClipActions(
   103→  entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[],

   105→): Promise<PendingClipAction[]> {
   106→  const actions: PendingClipAction[] = [];

   113→    const clip: VideoClip = {

   119→      playing: false,
   120→      generationId,
   121→    };
   122→
   123→    actions.push({ type: 'deferred_insert', clip });
   124→  }
   125→
   126→  return actions;
   127→}

   129→export async function consumePendingJoinClips(
   130→  options: ConsumePendingJoinClipsOptions = {},
   131→): Promise<OperationResult<PendingClipAction[]>> {
   132→  const projectId = options.projectId ?? null;
   133→  const readVideoDuration = options.readVideoDuration ?? getVideoDurationFromUrl;
   134→
   135→  try {
   136→    const userId = readUserIdFromStorage();
   137→
   138→    const inMemoryPending = consumeJoinClipsIntents({ projectId, userId });
   139→    if (inMemoryPending.length > 0) {
   140→      const now = Date.now();
   141→      const scopedRecentClips = inMemoryPending.filter(
   142→        (clip) =>
   143→          now - clip.timestamp < PENDING_CLIPS_TTL_MS
   144→          && isPendingJoinClipInScope(clip, { projectId, userId }),
   145→      );
   146→      if (scopedRecentClips.length === 0) {
   147→        localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   148→        return operationSuccess([]);
   149→      }
   150→
   151→      const actions = await toPendingClipActions(scopedRecentClips, readVideoDuration);
   152→      localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   153→      return operationSuccess(actions);

   156→    const pendingKeys = getPendingJoinClipsCandidateKeys({ projectId, userId });
   157→    const pendingSource = pendingKeys
   158→      .map((key) => ({ key, raw: localStorage.getItem(key) }))
   159→      .find((item) => typeof item.raw === 'string' && item.raw.length > 0);
   160→
   161→    if (!pendingSource || !pendingSource.raw) {
   162→      return operationSuccess([]);
   163→    }
   164→
   165→    const parsedPendingClips = parsePendingJoinClips(pendingSource.raw);
   166→    if (!parsedPendingClips) {
   167→      normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   168→        context: 'JoinClipsPage.pendingClipsInvalid',
   169→        showToast: false,
   170→        logData: { [REDACTED] },
   171→      });
   172→      localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);
   173→      return operationFailure(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   174→        policy: 'degrade',
   175→        errorCode: 'pending_join_clips_invalid_payload',
   176→        message: 'Invalid pending join clips payload',
   177→        recoverable: true,

   181→
   182→    if (parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0) {

   189→          invalidEntries: parsedPendingClips.invalidCount,

   191→      });

   202→    if (scopedRecentClips.length === 0) {

   224→  }
   225→}

   227→/**
   228→ * Apply pending clip actions to an existing clips array.
   229→ * Resolves each deferred action by filling the first available empty slot,
   230→ * or appending when no empty slots remain.
   231→ */
   232→export function applyPendingClipActions(
   233→  prevClips: VideoClip[],
   234→  actions: PendingClipAction[],
   235→): VideoClip[] {
   236→  let clips = [...prevClips];
   237→  // Track which indices have been filled by previous actions in this batch
   238→  const filledIndices = new Set<number>();
   239→
   240→  for (const action of actions) {
   241→    const emptyIndex = clips.findIndex(
   242→      (clip, idx) => !clip.url && !filledIndices.has(idx),
   243→    );
   244→
   245→    if (emptyIndex !== -1) {
   246→      clips = clips.map((clip, idx) =>
   247→        idx === emptyIndex
   248→          ? {
   249→              ...clip,
   250→              url: action.clip.url,
   251→              posterUrl: action.clip.posterUrl,
   252→              durationSeconds: action.clip.durationSeconds,
   253→              loaded: false,
   254→              playing: false,
   255→              generationId: action.clip.generationId,
   256→            }
   257→          : clip,
   258→      );
   259→      filledIndices.add(emptyIndex);
   260→    } else {
   261→      clips = [...clips, action.clip];
   262→    }
   263→  }
   264→
   265→  return clips;
   266→}

    29→export function preloadPosterImages(

    44→          img.src = url;

    10→  delayMs?: number;

    15→
    16→interface VariantInvalidationOptions {
    17→  reason: string;
    18→  generationId: string;
    19→  shotId?: string;
    20→  projectId?: string;
    21→  delayMs?: number;
    22→}
    23→
    24→type TimeoutStore = Map<string, ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>;
    25→
    26→const syncInvalidationTimeouts: TimeoutStore = new Map();
    27→interface VariantDelayEntry {
    28→  timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
    29→  settleCallbacks: Array<(shouldRun: boolean) => void>;
    30→}
    31→
    32→const variantInvalidationDelays = new Map<string, VariantDelayEntry>();
    33→
    34→function logInvalidationEvent(
    35→  _message: string,
    36→  _payload: Record<string, unknown>,
    37→): void {
    38→  // Intentionally empty — call sites kept for easy re-enablement during debugging
    39→}

    41→function buildInvalidationKey(shotId: string, options: InvalidationOptions): string {
    42→  const {
    43→    scope = 'all',
    44→    projectId = '',
    45→    includeShots = false,
    46→    includeProjectUnified = false,
    47→  } = options;
    48→  return [shotId, scope, projectId, includeShots ? 'shots' : '', includeProjectUnified ? 'unified' : ''].join('|');
    49→}
    50→
    51→function scheduleInvalidationExecution(
    52→  queryClient: QueryClient,
    53→  timeoutStore: TimeoutStore,
    54→  shotId: string,
    55→  options: InvalidationOptions,
    56→): void {
    57→  const [REDACTED](shotId, options);
    58→  const existingTimeout = timeoutStore.get(key);
    59→  if (existingTimeout) {
    60→    clearTimeout(existingTimeout);
    61→    timeoutStore.delete(key);
    62→  }
    63→
    64→  const execute = () => {
    65→    logInvalidationEvent('run', {
    66→      reason: options.reason,
    67→      shotId,
    68→      scope: options.scope ?? 'all',
    69→    });
    70→    performInvalidation(queryClient, shotId, options);
    71→    timeoutStore.delete(key);
    72→  };
    73→
    74→  if (options.delayMs && options.delayMs > 0) {
    75→    logInvalidationEvent('schedule', {
    76→      reason: options.reason,
    77→      shotId,
    78→      delayMs: options.delayMs,
    79→      scope: options.scope ?? 'all',
    80→    });
    81→    const timeout = setTimeout(execute, options.delayMs);
    82→    timeoutStore.set(key, timeout);
    83→    return;
    84→  }
    85→
    86→  execute();
    87→}
    88→
    89→async function waitForVariantDelay(
    90→  generationId: string,
    91→  reason: string,
    92→  delayMs?: number,
    93→): Promise<boolean> {
    94→  if (!delayMs || delayMs <= 0) {
    95→    return true;
    96→  }
    97→
    98→  const key = `variant:${generationId}`;
    99→  const existingDelay = variantInvalidationDelays.get(key);
   100→  if (existingDelay) {
   101→    clearTimeout(existingDelay.timeout);
   102→    variantInvalidationDelays.delete(key);
   103→    // Coalesce superseded callers and signal skip so they do not invalidate stale paths.
   104→    existingDelay.settleCallbacks.forEach((settle) => settle(false));
   105→  }
   106→
   107→  logInvalidationEvent('schedule_variant', {
   108→    reason,
   109→    generationId,
   110→    delayMs,
   111→  });
   112→
   113→  return await new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
   114→    const settleCallbacks = [resolve];
   115→    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
   116→      variantInvalidationDelays.delete(key);
   117→      settleCallbacks.forEach((settle) => settle(true));
   118→    }, delayMs);
   119→    variantInvalidationDelays.set(key, {
   120→      timeout,
   121→      settleCallbacks,
   122→    });
   123→  });
   124→}
   125→
   126→function performInvalidation(
   127→  queryClient: QueryClient,
   128→  shotId: string,
   129→  options: InvalidationOptions
   130→): void {
   131→  const {
   132→    scope = 'all',
   133→    includeShots = false,
   134→    projectId,
   135→    includeProjectUnified = false,
   136→  } = options;
   137→
   138→  if (scope === 'all' || scope === 'images') {
   139→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) });
   140→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) });
   141→  }
   142→
   143→  if (scope === 'all' || scope === 'metadata') {
   144→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) });
   145→  }
   146→
   147→  if (scope === 'all' || scope === 'counts') {
   148→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) });
   149→  }
   150→
   151→  if (includeShots && projectId) {
   152→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](projectId) });
   153→  }
   154→
   155→  if (includeProjectUnified && projectId) {
   156→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](projectId) });
   157→  }
   158→}
   159→
   160→export function useEnqueueGenerationsInvalidation() {
   161→  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
   162→  const timeoutRefs = useRef<TimeoutStore>(new Map());
   163→
   164→  return useCallback((shotId: string, options: InvalidationOptions) => {
   165→    scheduleInvalidationExecution(queryClient, timeoutRefs.current, shotId, options);
   166→  }, [queryClient]);
   167→}
   168→
   169→export function enqueueGenerationsInvalidation(
   170→  queryClient: QueryClient,
   171→  shotId: string,
   172→  options: InvalidationOptions
   173→): void {
   174→  scheduleInvalidationExecution(queryClient, syncInvalidationTimeouts, shotId, options);
   175→}
   176→
   177→export function invalidateAllShotGenerations(queryClient: QueryClient): void {
   178→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({
   179→    predicate: (query) => query.queryKey[0] === queryKeys.generations.byShotAll[0],
   180→  });
   181→}
   182→
   183→export async function enqueueVariantInvalidation(
   184→  queryClient: QueryClient,
   185→  options: VariantInvalidationOptions
   186→): Promise<void> {
   187→  const { generationId, shotId, projectId } = options;
   188→
   189→  const shouldRunInvalidation = await waitForVariantDelay(
   190→    generationId,
   191→    options.reason,
   192→    options.delayMs,
   193→  );
   194→  if (!shouldRunInvalidation) {
   195→    logInvalidationEvent('skip_variant', {
   196→      reason: options.reason,
   197→      generationId,
   198→      shotId,
   199→      projectId,
   200→    });
   201→    return;
   202→  }
   203→  logInvalidationEvent('run_variant', {
   204→    reason: options.reason,
   205→    generationId,
   206→    shotId,
   207→    projectId,
   208→  });
   209→
   210→  // Specific generation + variants
   211→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](generationId) });
   212→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](generationId) });
   213→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED] });
   214→
   215→  if (shotId) {
   216→    await queryClient.refetchQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) });
   217→  }
   218→
   219→  // Scoped: only invalidate project or fall back to all
   220→  if (projectId) {
   221→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](projectId) });
   222→  } else {
   223→    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED] });
   224→  }
   225→
   226→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED] });
   227→
   228→  // Segments may reference this variant as source
   229→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({
   230→    predicate: (query) => query.queryKey[0] === queryKeys.segments.childrenAll[0],
   231→  });
   232→
   233→  queryClient.invalidateQueries({
   234→    predicate: (query) => query.queryKey[0] === queryKeys.segments.sourceSlotAll[0],
   235→  });
   236→}
   237→

   239→export const useInvalidateGenerations = useEnqueueGenerationsInvalidation;

   241→export const invalidateGenerationsSync = enqueueGenerationsInvalidation;
   242→/** @deprecated Use `enqueueVariantInvalidation` for explicit queue semantics. */
   243→export const invalidateVariantChange = enqueueVariantInvalidation;

/**
 * Types for ShotImagesEditor and its sub-components.
 */

import type { GenerationRow, Shot } from '@/domains/generation/types';
import type { VideoMetadata } from '@/shared/lib/media/videoUploader';
import type { StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata } from '@/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages';

// =============================================================================
// Main Component Props
// =============================================================================

interface ShotImagesEditorDisplayOptions {
  /** Controls whether internal UI should render the skeleton */
  isModeReady: boolean;
  /** Optional error text shown at the top of the card */
  settingsError?: string | null;
  /** Whether the UI is currently on a mobile breakpoint */
  isMobile: boolean;
  /** Current generation mode */
  generationMode: 'batch' | 'timeline' | 'by-pair';
  /** Callback to switch modes */
  onGenerationModeChange: (mode: 'batch' | 'timeline' | 'by-pair') => void;
  /** Number of columns for batch mode grid */
  columns: 2 | 3 | 4 | 6;
  /** Skeleton component to show while loading */
  skeleton: React.ReactNode;
  /** Read-only mode - disables all interactions */
  readOnly?: boolean;
  /** Project aspect ratio for display */
  projectAspectRatio?: string;
  /** Project-level cache: whether this shot has structure videos (for skeleton) */
  cachedHasStructureVideo?: boolean;
  /** Maximum frame limit for timeline gaps (77 when smoothContinuations enabled, 81 otherwise) */
  maxFrameLimit?: number;
  /** Whether smooth continuations is enabled - used to compact timeline gaps when toggled */
  smoothContinuations?: boolean;
  /** Shared selected output parent ID (for syncing FinalVideoSection with SegmentOutputStrip) */
  selectedOutputId?: string | null;
  /** Callback when selected output changes */
  onSelectedOutputChange?: (id: string | null) => void;
}

interface ShotImagesEditorImageState {
  /** Selected shot id */
  selectedShotId: string;
  /** Optional preloaded images (for read-only/share views) - bypasses database queries */
  preloadedImages?: GenerationRow[];
  /** Project id for video uploads */
  projectId?: string;
  /** Shot name for download filename */
  shotName?: string;
  /** Frame spacing (frames between key-frames) */
  batchVideoFrames: number;
  /** Map of pending frame positions coming from server */
  pendingPositions: Map<string, number>;
  /** Count of unpositioned generations */
  unpositionedGenerationsCount: number;
  /** File input key for resetting */
  fileInputKey: number;
  /** Whether currently uploading image */
  isUploadingImage: boolean;
  /** Upload progress (0-100) */
  uploadProgress?: number;
  /** ID of image currently being duplicated */
  duplicatingImageId?: string | null;
  /** ID of image that was just duplicated (for success indication) */
  duplicateSuccessImageId?: string | null;
  /** Default prompt for timeline pairs (from existing generation settings) */
  defaultPrompt?: string;
  onDefaultPromptChange?: (prompt: string) => void;
  /** Default negative prompt for timeline pairs (from existing generation settings) */
  defaultNegativePrompt?: string;
  onDefaultNegativePromptChange?: (prompt: string) => void;

  // Structure video props - legacy compatibility interface.
  // Internal consumers should prefer `structureVideos` and derive these via adapter helpers.
  primaryStructureVideoPath?: string | null;
  primaryStructureVideoMetadata?: VideoMetadata | null;
  primaryStructureVideoTreatment?: 'adjust' | 'clip';
  primaryStructureVideoMotionStrength?: number;
  primaryStructureVideoType?: 'uni3c' | 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth';
  /** Uni3C end percent (only used when primaryStructureVideoType is 'uni3c') */
  primaryStructureVideoUni3cEndPercent?: number;

  // Canonical structure video contract
  structureVideos?: StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata[];
  isStructureVideoLoading?: boolean;

  /** Audio strip props */
  audioUrl?: string | null;
  audioMetadata?: { duration: number; name?: string } | null;
}

interface ShotImagesEditorEditActions {
  /** Reordering callback – receives ordered ids and optionally the dragged item ID */
  onImageReorder: (orderedIds: string[], draggedItemId?: string) => void;
  /** Timeline frame positions change */
  onFramePositionsChange: (newPositions: Map<string, number>) => void;
  /** Callback when external images are dropped on the timeline */
  onFileDrop: (files: File[], targetFrame?: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Callback when generations are dropped from GenerationsPane onto the timeline */
  onGenerationDrop?: (generationId: string, imageUrl: string, thumbUrl: string | undefined, targetFrame?: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Callback when external images are dropped on batch mode grid */
  onBatchFileDrop?: (files: File[], targetPosition?: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Callback when generations are dropped from GenerationsPane onto batch mode grid */
  onBatchGenerationDrop?: (generationId: string, imageUrl: string, thumbUrl: string | undefined, targetPosition?: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Callback when pending position is applied */
  onPendingPositionApplied: (generationId: string) => void;
  /** Image deletion callback - id is shot_generations.id (unique per entry) */
  onImageDelete: (id: string) => void;
  /** Batch image deletion callback - ids are shot_generations.id values */
  onBatchImageDelete?: (ids: string[]) => void;
  /** Image duplication callback - id is shot_generations.id */
  onImageDuplicate?: (id: string, timeline_frame: number) => void;
  /** Callback to open unpositioned pane */
  onOpenUnpositionedPane: () => void;
  /** Image upload callback */
  onImageUpload: (files: File[]) => Promise<void>;

  onPrimaryStructureVideoInputChange?: (
    videoPath: string | null,
    metadata: VideoMetadata | null,
    treatment: 'adjust' | 'clip',
    motionStrength: number,
    structureType: 'uni3c' | 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth',
    resourceId?: string,
  ) => void;
  /** Callback for changing uni3c end percent */
  onUni3cEndPercentChange?: (value: number) => void;

  onAddStructureVideo?: (video: StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata) => void;
  onUpdateStructureVideo?: (index: number, updates: Partial<StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata>) => void;
  onRemoveStructureVideo?: (index: number) => void;
  /** Set the entire structure videos array (for overlap resolution) */
  onSetStructureVideos?: (videos: StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata[]) => void;

  onAudioChange?: (
    audioUrl: string | null,
    metadata: { duration: number; name?: string } | null,
  ) => void;

  /** Callback when selection state changes */
  onSelectionChange?: (hasSelection: boolean) => void;

  /** Callback to notify parent of drag state changes - used to suppress query refetches during drag */
  onDragStateChange?: (isDragging: boolean) => void;
  /** Callback when single-image duration changes (for single-image video generation) */
  onTrailingDurationChange?: (durationFrames: number | undefined) => void;
}

interface ShotImagesEditorShotWorkflow {
  /** Shot management for external generation viewing */
  allShots?: Shot[];
  onShotChange?: (shotId: string) => void;
  onAddToShot?: (shotId: string, generationId: string, position?: number) => Promise<void>;
  onAddToShotWithoutPosition?: (shotId: string, generationId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  onCreateShot?: (name: string) => Promise<string>;
  onNewShotFromSelection?: (selectedIds: string[]) => Promise<string | void>;
}

export interface ShotImagesEditorProps {
  displayOptions: ShotImagesEditorDisplayOptions;
  imageState: ShotImagesEditorImageState;
  editActions: ShotImagesEditorEditActions;
  shotWorkflow: ShotImagesEditorShotWorkflow;
}

export type ShotImagesEditorResolvedProps =
  & ShotImagesEditorDisplayOptions
  & ShotImagesEditorImageState
  & ShotImagesEditorEditActions
  & ShotImagesEditorShotWorkflow;

export function resolveShotImagesEditorProps(props: ShotImagesEditorProps): ShotImagesEditorResolvedProps {
  return {
    ...props.displayOptions,
    ...props.imageState,
    ...props.editActions,
    ...props.shotWorkflow,
  };
}

// =============================================================================
// Preview Together Dialog Types
// =============================================================================

export interface PreviewSegment {
  hasVideo: boolean;
  videoUrl: string | null;
  thumbUrl: string | null;
  startImageUrl: string | null;
  endImageUrl: string | null;
  index: number;
  durationFromFrames: number;
}

         Current callers of normalizeAndReportError ALL pass showToast: false — so the silent drop is harmless today. But the options type accepting toastTitle/showToast is misleading and could cause bugs if someone copies a call pattern from normalizeAndPresentError.
         
         The fix is correct: remove toastTitle and showToast from RuntimeErrorReportOptions. This narrows the type to just ErrorReportOptions (which has context, logData, onError). All current callers only use { context, showToast: false } — they would get a compile error on showToast: false, which they should just remove since reporting is already silent by design.
         
         Regarding renaming: normalizeAndReportError is NOT re-exported from errorHandling/index.ts (checked — it only exports normalizeAndPresentError, reportError, reportAndRethrow, reportRecoverableError, withRecoverableHandling). All 8 callers import directly from runtimeErrorReporting.ts. A rename is viable but optional — the bigger win is fixing the options type.

         Verified. src/shared/hooks/useShareGeneration.ts (410 lines).

         The unstable dep is on line 401: useCallback deps array includes 'options' (the full object). Since callers pass options inline (e.g., MediaGalleryItem.tsx line 131 passes no options, VideoItem.tsx line 78-81 passes inline { initialShareSlug }), the object reference changes every render, defeating useCallback.
         
         However, the actual impact is LOW: handleShare is an async click handler (not passed as a dep to other hooks), so re-creation on each render causes no cascading invalidation. The main cost is unnecessary closure re-creation.
         
         The useEffect on line 79-82 has options?.initialShareSlug in deps — this correctly extracts the primitive value. No issue there.
         
         Fix (as described): destructure at the top of the hook body:
         const { initialShareSlug, onShareCreated } = options ?? {};
         Then replace options?.initialShareSlug with initialShareSlug in the useEffect dep (line 82), and options?.onShareCreated?. with onShareCreated?. on line 373. Replace 'options' with 'onShareCreated' in the useCallback deps (line 401). The 'toast' in deps (line 401) is also suspicious — toast is imported as a function, not a hook return, so it is stable and could be removed from deps.

   - **Desloppify triage flow**: 5-stage ceremony (OBSERVE → REFLECT → ORGANIZE → ENRICH → COMMIT) forcing AI agents to plan before executing
   - **Fold-confirm**: Pass `--attestation` to a later stage to auto-confirm the prior stage inline
   - **Shallow steps**: Steps lacking `detail` or `issue_refs` — now a hard blocker at enrich stage
   - **Activity tracking**: `count_log_activity_since()` counts execution_log entries by action type since a timestamp
   - **Cascade clearing**: When a stage is re-recorded with new data, later stage confirmations are invalidated
   - **Data-state gates vs text-quality gates**: Structural checks (clusters enriched, issues clustered) are real enforcement; text checks (report length, attestation content) are speed bumps
   - **verified_files**: Proposed new step field requiring enrichers to list source files they actually read

   855→      case 'user': return 'users';
   856→      case 'project': return 'projects';
   857→      case 'shot': return 'shots';
   858→    }
   859→    throw new Error(`Invalid settings scope: ${String(scope)}`);
   860→  }
   861→
   862→The switch exhaustively covers all values of SettingsScopeIdentifier ('user' | 'project' | 'shot'). The throw on line 16 is unreachable in TypeScript. However, at runtime (JS), if a non-typed value were passed, the throw would fire. This is a common defensive pattern.
   863→
   864→VERDICT: VALID but TRIVIAL. The best fix is replacing the throw with a never assertion: const _exhaustive: never = scope; This provides compile-time safety (catches missing cases when new scopes are added) AND is more idiomatic TypeScript. The throw is not wrong per se - it's a runtime safety net - but the never pattern is strictly better because it catches the problem at compile time rather than runtime.

## Desloppify Plan Readability Report

### 1-Sentence Summaries (from quick scan of cluster names + descriptions only)

| Cluster | Quick Summary (titles/name only) | Accurate after reading details? |
|---------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **security-auth-fixes** | Fix auth/JWT holes in edge functions. | Yes -- exactly right. 2 steps: add JWT verification, migrate 14 edge functions to consistent auth wrapper. |
| **architecture-boundaries** | Restructure the oversized shared/ directory. | Mostly -- the name says "boundaries" but the work is really "decompose shared/ mega-package." Name undersells the scope. |
| **contract-dedup** | Remove duplicated helper functions. | Partially -- "contract" is misleading. It's about duplicate implementations (deriveInputImages, asRecord, etc.), not API contracts. I expected interface/schema dedup. |
| **incomplete-migrations** | Finish or remove half-done code migrations. | Yes -- dead aliases, compat shims, legacy field duality. Name is accurate. |
| **error-handling** | Fix inconsistent error handling. | Yes -- 4 specific silent-catch fixes + an ADR on OperationResult pattern. Clear. |
| **design-coherence** | Fix bloated hooks and components. | Partially confused -- overlaps heavily with abstraction-bloat. "Design coherence" made me expect visual/UI design issues (spacing, color consistency). It's actually about god-hooks and prop bloat. |
| **abstraction-bloat** | Remove unnecessary abstraction layers. | Yes -- forwarding hooks, pure aliases, reshaping layers. Name is clear. |
| **convention-cleanup** | Fix naming/export/style inconsistencies. | Yes -- export patterns, directory naming, comment cleanup. Straightforward. |
| **type-safety-and-infra** | Improve TypeScript types + fix infra issues. | Partially -- it's a grab-bag. Typed enums, unsafe casts, module-scope side effects, lazy loading, a dependency bump, and a logic bug. "Infra" hides too much variety. |
| **test-strategy** | Add missing tests. | Yes, but "strategy" oversells it. It's 5 specific test-writing tasks, not a testing strategy document. |

### Top 10 Readability Improvements Needed

**1. No status on any step.** All 76 steps have no status field. There is zero way to tell what's done vs. pending at a glance. This is the single biggest gap -- a PM cannot track progress.

**2. Step titles are sentences, not titles.** Many are 170-270 characters long -- full implementation instructions embedded in the title. Example: "Add JWT signature verification to the auth path that currently decodes without verifying -- check supabase/functions/_shared/ for the verify_jwt=false configuration and add proper JWKS validation" (194 chars). Titles should be under 80 chars; implementation detail belongs in the detail field.

**3. No effort estimates anywhere.** There is no size, points, hours, or t-shirt sizing on any cluster or step. "Audit all 31 edge functions" sits next to "Delete compat/errorHandler.ts re-exports." A PM cannot estimate total scope or plan sprints.

**4. "design-coherence" and "abstraction-bloat" overlap.** Both are about decomposing oversized hooks. The distinction (god-hooks vs. forwarding hooks) is too subtle for a plan overview. A VP would ask "why are there two refactoring clusters?"

**5. "contract-dedup" name is misleading.** "Contract" suggests API interfaces or schemas. The actual work is merging duplicate utility functions. "duplicate-implementations" or "dedup-utilities" would be clearer.

**6. "type-safety-and-infra" is a junk drawer.** It mixes type safety (4 steps), module-scope side effects (3 steps), a dependency bump, a lazy-load task, and a logic bug. These are 3-4 distinct concerns stapled together.

**7. No cluster-level completion metric.** Clusters have `issue_ids` counts (2-15) and `action_steps` counts (2-12) but no "X of Y done" indicator. The `plan_start_scores` (strict: 38.8, overall: 38.8) exist only at the plan level with no per-cluster breakdown.

**8. Priority numbers lack context.** Priorities range 1-7 but there is no legend explaining the scale, no labels like "critical/high/medium/low," and no grouping by priority tier. You have to mentally sort 10 numbers.

**9. Queue order is empty for manual clusters.** `queue_order` contains only workflow meta-steps, not the cluster execution sequence. Despite having priority numbers, there is no explicit ordering of which cluster to tackle first vs. last.

**10. "test-strategy" is named like a planning exercise but contains 5 concrete test-writing tasks.** The name sets expectations of a strategy document; the content is a backlog of test gaps.

### VP-Presentable vs. Too Granular

**Present to a VP (strategic, high-impact, easy to explain):**
- **security-auth-fixes** (priority 1) -- "We have unverified JWTs in production edge functions." Immediate executive attention.
- **architecture-boundaries** (priority 4) -- "67% of our code is in a single shared/ directory with circular dependencies." Explains systemic velocity drag.
- **incomplete-migrations** (priority 2) -- "We have dead code and half-finished migrations creating confusion." Easy to understand tech debt narrative.
- **error-handling** (priority 6) -- "Users aren't seeing error messages when things fail." Clear user impact.

**Too granular for a VP (engineering-internal concerns):**
- **contract-dedup** -- "We have two versions of deriveInputImages." VP eyes glaze over.
- **design-coherence** -- "useGenerationsPaneController returns 60+ values." Meaningless without codebase context.
- **abstraction-bloat** -- "useShotEditorLayoutPayloadModel forwards 340 lines." Same problem.
- **convention-cleanup** -- Export patterns and comment cleanup. Pure housekeeping.
- **type-safety-and-infra** -- Mixed bag of TypeScript nits and module-scope fixes.
- **test-strategy** -- 5 specific test tasks. Present as part of a broader quality narrative, not standalone.

**For VP presentation, I'd roll up the 10 clusters into 4 themes:**
1. Security (security-auth-fixes)
2. Dead code & tech debt (incomplete-migrations, convention-cleanup)
3. Architecture & maintainability (architecture-boundaries, contract-dedup, design-coherence, abstraction-bloat)
4. Reliability (error-handling, type-safety-and-infra, test-strategy)

### Overall Glanceability Score: 4/10

**What works:** Cluster names are mostly intuitive (7/10 gave correct first impressions). Priority numbers exist. Descriptions are information-dense.

**What fails:** No progress tracking whatsoever. No effort sizing. Step titles double as implementation specs. Two clusters overlap confusingly. One cluster is a junk drawer. No visual hierarchy beyond a bare priority integer. A PM opening this for the first time cannot answer "how much work is left?" or "what should we do this week?" without reading every detail field.

You are a process analyst investigating WHY the desloppify triage process failed to catch quality issues in the plan. This is a meta-analysis — not about the code, but about the triage process itself.

## Background

The desloppify triage flow has 5 stages: OBSERVE → REFLECT → ORGANIZE → ENRICH → COMMIT. 

During triage on this codebase (reigh), the following problems were discovered AFTER triage completed:
1. Step details written from issue summaries, not actual source code — leading to wrong file paths, wrong function counts, nonexistent functions referenced
2. 3 of 8 steps in abstraction-bloat were false positives (hooks already well-decomposed)
3. A step in design-coherence referenced a completely wrong file path (component doesn't exist where claimed)
4. convention-cleanup step 7 had the recommendation BACKWARDS (wrong dominant pattern identified)
5. Steps mixed trivial fixes with multi-day refactors with no effort indication
6. Clusters had overlapping concerns but no cross-references
7. No verification that enrichment agents actually read source files

## Your task

1. Read the desloppify triage code to understand what each stage actually checks:
   - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_commands.py` — the stage handlers
   - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py` — validation gates
   - `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/confirmations.py` — confirmation checks

2. For each failure type above, trace back through the triage stages and identify:
   - Which stage SHOULD have caught this?
   - What check exists (or doesn't) at that stage?
   - Is the check structural (data-state gate) or textual (speed bump)?
   - What would need to change to actually catch it?

3. Categorize the root causes:
   - **Process gaps**: stages that don't check for something they should
   - **Enforcement gaps**: checks that exist but are advisory-only (warnings not blockers)
   - **Tooling gaps**: things that can't be checked without additional tooling (e.g., "did the enricher actually read source files?")
   - **Scope gaps**: things the triage process was never designed to catch

   387→def _cmd_stage_enrich(

   403→

   232→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   233→    """Return (cluster_name, bare_count, total_count) for clusters with steps lacking detail."""
   234→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   235→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   236→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   237→            continue
   238→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   239→        if not steps:
   240→            continue
   241→        bare = sum(
   242→            1 for s in steps
   243→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   244→        )
   245→        if bare > 0:
   246→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   247→    return results
   248→

   511→) -> bool:
   512→    if has_only_additions:
   513→        _print_new_issues_since_last(si)
   514→        return True
   515→    if "observe" not in stages:
   516→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: observe stage not complete.", "red"))
   517→        print(colorize("  You must read issues first.", "dim"))
   518→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   519→        return False
   520→    if "reflect" not in stages:
   521→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: reflect stage not complete.", "red"))
   522→        print(colorize("  You must compare against completed work first.", "dim"))
   523→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   524→        return False
   525→    return True
   526→
   527→
   528→def _confirm_note_valid(note: str | None) -> bool:
   529→    if not note:
   530→        print(colorize("  --note is required for confirm-existing.", "red"))
   531→        print(colorize('  Explain why the existing plan is still valid (min 100 chars).', "dim"))
   532→        return False
   533→    if len(note) < 100:
   534→        print(colorize(f"  Note too short: {len(note)} chars (minimum 100).", "red"))
   535→        return False
   536→    return True
   537→
   538→
   539→def _resolve_confirm_existing_strategy(
   540→    strategy: str | None,
   541→    *,
   542→    has_only_additions: bool,
   543→    meta: dict,
   544→) -> str | None:
   545→    if strategy:
   546→        return strategy
   547→    if has_only_additions:
   548→        return "same"
   549→    print(colorize("  --strategy is required.", "red"))
   550→    existing = meta.get("strategy_summary", "")
   551→    if existing:
   552→        print(colorize('  Use --strategy "same" to keep it, or provide a new summary.', "dim"))
   553→    return None
   554→
   555→
   556→def _confirm_strategy_valid(strategy: str) -> bool:
   557→    if strategy.strip().lower() == "same":
   558→        return True
   559→    if len(strategy.strip()) >= 200:
   560→        return True
   561→    print(colorize(f"  Strategy too short: {len(strategy.strip())} chars (minimum 200).", "red"))
   562→    return False
   563→
   564→
   565→def _confirmed_text_or_error(
   566→    *,
   567→    plan: dict,
   568→    state: dict,
   569→    confirmed: str | None,
   570→) -> str | None:
   571→    if confirmed and len(confirmed.strip()) >= _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   572→        return confirmed.strip()
   573→    print(colorize("  Current plan:", "bold"))
   574→    show_plan_summary(plan, state)
   575→    if confirmed:
   576→        print(
   577→            colorize(
   578→                f"\n  --confirmed text too short ({len(confirmed.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   579→                "red",
   580→            )
   581→        )
   582→    print(colorize('\n  Add --confirmed "I validate this plan..." to proceed.', "dim"))
   583→    return None
   584→
   585→
   586→def _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note: str, si) -> bool:
   587→    new_ids = si.new_since_last
   588→    if not new_ids:
   589→        return True
   590→    valid_ids = set(si.open_issues.keys())
   591→    cited = extract_issue_citations(note, valid_ids)
   592→    new_cited = cited & new_ids
   593→    if new_cited:
   594→        return True
   595→    print(colorize("  Note must cite at least 1 new/changed issue.", "red"))
   596→    print(colorize(f"  {len(new_ids)} new issue(s) since last triage:", "dim"))
   597→    for fid in sorted(new_ids)[:5]:

   599→    if len(new_ids) > 5:
   600→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(new_ids) - 5} more", "dim"))
   601→    return False

1→"""Stage-gate and coverage helpers for triage command handlers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine.plan import TRIAGE_IDS
     7→
     8→
     9→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:
    10→    """Require at least one triage stage ID to be present in queue for an action."""
    11→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    12→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
    13→        return True
    14→    print(colorize(f"  No triage stage in the queue — nothing to {action}.", "yellow"))
    15→    return False
    16→
    17→
    18→def _validate_stage_report(
    19→    report: str | None,
    20→    *,
    21→    stage: str,
    22→    min_chars: int,
    23→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    24→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    25→) -> str | None:
    26→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    27→    if not report:
    28→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    29→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    30→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    31→        return None
    32→    cleaned = report.strip()
    33→    if len(cleaned) < min_chars:
    34→        print(
    35→            colorize(
    36→                f"  Report too short: {len(cleaned)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).",
    37→                "red",
    38→            )
    39→        )
    40→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    41→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    42→        return None
    43→    return cleaned
    44→
    45→
    46→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    47→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    48→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    49→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    50→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    51→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    52→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id not in TRIAGE_IDS]
    53→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    54→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters
    55→
    56→
    57→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    58→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment.
    59→
    60→    Requirements:
    61→    - Every cluster needs a description and at least one action_step.
    62→    - Small clusters (< 5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue,
    63→      so each item has a concrete plan. Large clusters (>= 5) just need
    64→      steps overall (cluster-level plan is sufficient).
    65→    """
    66→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    67→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    68→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    69→            continue
    70→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    71→            continue
    72→        missing: list[str] = []
    73→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    74→            missing.append("description")
    75→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
    76→        issue_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    77→        if not steps:
    78→            missing.append("action_steps")
    79→        elif issue_count < 5 and len(steps) < issue_count:
    80→            missing.append(
    81→                f"action_steps (have {len(steps)}, need >= {issue_count} for small cluster)"
    82→            )
    83→        if missing:
    84→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    85→    return gaps
    86→
    87→
    88→def _unclustered_review_issues(plan: dict, state: dict | None = None) -> list[str]:
    89→    """Return review issue IDs that aren't in any manual cluster.
    90→
    91→    When *state* is provided, uses open review/concerns issues from state
    92→    (the canonical source). Falls back to scanning queue_order for backwards
    93→    compatibility.
    94→    """
    95→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    96→    clustered_ids: set[str] = set()
    97→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    98→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
    99→            clustered_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   100→
   101→    if state is not None:
   102→        review_ids = [
   103→            fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   104→            if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   105→        ]
   106→    else:
   107→        review_ids = [
   108→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   109→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")
   110→            and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   111→        ]
   112→
   113→    return [fid for fid in review_ids if fid not in clustered_ids]
   114→

    43→    """Complete triage — requires organize stage (or confirm-existing path)."""

    56→    state = resolved_services.command_runtime(args).state

    59→    # Require organize stage confirmed

    61→        plan=plan,

    65→        return
    66→

    68→    if not _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete(
    69→        plan=plan,
    70→        stages=stages,
    71→        attestation=attestation,
    72→    ):
    73→        return
    74→
    75→    # Require enrich stage confirmed
    76→    if not _require_enrich_stage_for_complete(

    78→        meta=meta,

    83→    # Fold-confirm: auto-confirm enrich if attestation provided

   145→
   146→    print_user_message(
   147→        "Hey — triage is done. Run `desloppify next` and start"
   148→        " executing the plan. Don't stop until you're done —"
   149→        " unless I've told you otherwise, just go."
   150→    )
   151→
   152→
   153→def _cmd_confirm_existing(
   154→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   155→    *,
   156→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   157→) -> None:
   158→    """Fast-track: confirm existing plan structure is still valid."""
   159→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   160→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   161→    strategy: str | None = getattr(args, "strategy", None)
   162→    confirmed: str | None = getattr(args, "confirmed", None)
   163→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   164→
   165→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   166→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to confirm.", "yellow"))
   167→        return
   168→
   169→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   170→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   171→
   172→    # Require a prior completed triage — can't skip the full flow on first run
   173→    if not _require_prior_strategy_for_confirm(meta):
   174→        return
   175→
   176→    # Determine if this is a light-path (additions only) or full ceremony
   177→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   178→    state = runtime.state
   179→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   180→    has_only_additions = bool(si.new_since_last) and not si.resolved_since_last
   181→
   182→    if not _confirm_existing_stages_valid(
   183→        stages=stages,
   184→        has_only_additions=has_only_additions,
   185→        si=si,
   186→    ):
   187→        return
   188→
   189→    # Require existing enriched clusters
   190→    clusters_with_issues = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
   191→    if not clusters_with_issues:
   192→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: no clusters with issues exist.", "red"))
   193→        print(colorize("  Use the full organize flow instead.", "dim"))
   194→        return
   195→
   196→    # Require note
   197→    if not _confirm_note_valid(note):
   198→        return
   199→
   200→    # Require strategy (default to "same" on light path)
   201→    strategy = _resolve_confirm_existing_strategy(
   202→        strategy,
   203→        has_only_additions=has_only_additions,
   204→        meta=meta,
   205→    )
   206→    if strategy is None:
   207→        return
   208→
   209→    # Strategy length check (unless "same")
   210→    if not _confirm_strategy_valid(strategy):
   211→        return
   212→
   213→    # Require --confirmed with plan review
   214→    confirmed_text = _confirmed_text_or_error(
   215→        plan=plan,
   216→        state=state,
   217→        confirmed=confirmed,
   218→    )
   219→    if confirmed_text is None:
   220→        return
   221→
   222→    # Validate: note cites at least 1 new/changed issue (if there are any)
   223→    if not _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note, si):
   224→        return
   225→
   226→    # Record organize as confirmed-existing and complete
   227→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   228→    _record_confirm_existing_completion(
   229→        stages=stages,
   230→        note=note,
   231→        issue_count=len(clusters_with_issues),
   232→        confirmed_text=confirmed_text,
   233→    )
   234→
   235→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   236→        plan,
   237→        "triage_confirm_existing",
   238→        actor="user",
   239→        detail={"confirmed_text": confirmed_text},
   240→    )
   241→
   242→    apply_completion(args, plan, strategy, services=resolved_services)
   243→    print(colorize("  Confirmed existing plan — triage complete.", "green"))
   244→
   245→
   246→def cmd_triage_complete(
   247→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   248→    *,
   249→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   250→) -> None:
   251→    """Public entrypoint for triage completion."""
   252→    _cmd_triage_complete(args, services=services)
   253→
   254→
   255→def cmd_confirm_existing(
   256→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   257→    *,
   258→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   259→) -> None:
   260→    """Public entrypoint for confirm-existing completion path."""
   261→    _cmd_confirm_existing(args, services=services)
   262→
   263→
   264→__all__ = [
   265→    "cmd_confirm_existing",
   266→    "cmd_triage_complete",
   267→    "_cmd_confirm_existing",
   268→    "_cmd_triage_complete",
   269→]
   270→

    37→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    38→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    39→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    40→    if plan is not None:
    41→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    42→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    43→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    44→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    45→                all_ids.append(fid)
    46→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    47→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    48→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    49→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    50→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    51→
    52→    for pattern in patterns:
    53→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    54→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    55→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    56→
    57→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    58→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    59→            if suggestions:
    60→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    61→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    62→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    63→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    64→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    65→            continue
    66→
    67→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    68→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    69→        for fid in all_ids:
    70→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    71→                suggestions.append(fid)
    72→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    73→                suggestions.append(fid)

   158→
   159→    # Check for overlap with other manual clusters
   160→    member_set = set(issue_ids)
   161→    for other_name, other_cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   162→        if other_name == cluster_name or other_cluster.get("auto"):
   163→            continue
   164→        other_ids = set(other_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   165→        if not other_ids:
   166→            continue
   167→        overlap = member_set & other_ids
   168→        if len(overlap) > len(other_ids) * 0.5:
   169→            print(colorize(
   170→                f"  Warning: {len(overlap)} issue(s) also in cluster '{other_name}' "
   171→                f"({len(overlap)}/{len(other_ids)} = {int(len(overlap)/len(other_ids)*100)}% overlap).",
   172→                "yellow",
   173→            ))
   174→
   175→    append_log_entry(
   176→        plan, "cluster_add", issue_ids=issue_ids, cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   177→    )
   178→    save_plan(plan)
   179→    print(colorize(f"  Added {count} item(s) to cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   180→

   193→    if not issue_ids:

   195→        _print_pattern_hints()
   196→        _suggest_close_matches(state, plan, patterns)

   214→    print(colorize(f"  Removed {count} item(s) from cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))

   231→
   232→def _resolve_item_position(
   233→    position: str,
   234→    target: str | None,
   235→    item_ids: list[str],
   236→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   237→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   238→    cluster_name: str,
   239→    state: dict,
   240→    plan: dict,
   241→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   242→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   243→
   244→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   245→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   246→    """
   247→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   248→
   249→    if position == "top":
   250→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   251→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   252→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   253→            return None
   254→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   255→
   256→    if position == "bottom":
   257→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   258→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   259→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   260→            return None
   261→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   262→
   263→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   264→        if target is None:
   265→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   266→            return None
   267→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   268→        if not target_ids:
   269→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   270→            return None
   271→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   272→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   273→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   274→            return None
   275→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   276→
   277→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   278→        if target is None:
   279→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   280→            return None
   281→        try:
   282→            offset = int(target)
   283→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   284→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   285→            return None
   286→        return (position, None, offset)
   287→
   288→    return (position, None, None)
   289→
   290→
   291→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   292→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   293→    plan: dict,
   294→    clusters: dict,
   295→    cluster_names: list[str],
   296→    position: str,
   297→    target: str | None,
   298→    item_pattern: str,
   299→) -> None:
   300→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   301→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   302→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   303→        return
   304→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   305→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   306→
   307→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   308→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   309→    if not item_ids:
   310→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   311→        return
   312→    for fid in item_ids:
   313→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   314→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   315→            return
   316→
   317→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   318→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   319→
   320→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   321→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   322→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   323→    )
   324→    if result is None:
   325→        return
   326→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   327→
   328→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   329→    append_log_entry(
   330→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   331→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   332→    )
   333→    save_plan(plan)
   334→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   335→
   336→
   337→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   338→    plan: dict,
   339→    clusters: dict,
   340→    cluster_names: list[str],
   341→    position: str,
   342→    target: str | None,
   343→) -> None:
   344→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   345→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   346→
   347→    offset = None
   348→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   349→        try:
   350→            offset = int(target)
   351→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   353→            return
   354→        target = None
   355→
   356→    seen: set[str] = set()
   357→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   358→    for name in cluster_names:
   359→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   360→            if fid not in seen:
   361→                seen.add(fid)
   362→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   363→
   364→    if not all_member_ids:
   365→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   369→    append_log_entry(
   370→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   371→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   372→    )
   373→    save_plan(plan)
   374→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   376→
   377→
   378→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   379→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   380→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   381→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   382→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   383→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   384→
   385→    plan = load_plan()
   386→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   387→
   388→    # Validate all names exist
   389→    for name in cluster_names:
   390→        if name not in clusters:
   391→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   392→            return
   393→
   394→    if item_pattern is not None:
   395→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   396→    else:
   397→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)
   398→

   421→def _print_step(i: int, step: str | dict) -> None:
   422→    """Print a single step with title, detail, refs, and done status."""
   423→    if isinstance(step, str):
   424→        print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))
   425→        return
   426→    done = step.get("done", False)
   427→    marker = "[x]" if done else "[ ]"
   428→    title = step.get("title", "")
   429→    print(f"    {i}. {marker} {title}")
   430→    if done:
   431→        print(colorize("         (completed)", "dim"))
   432→        return
   433→    detail = step.get("detail", "")
   434→    if detail:
   435→        for line in detail.splitlines():
   436→            print(colorize(f"         {line}", "dim"))
   437→    refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
   438→    if refs:
   439→        print(colorize(f"         Refs: {', '.join(refs)}", "dim"))

   442→def _cmd_cluster_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

   449→
   450→    # Header

   495→    print(colorize(f"    Skip:         desloppify plan skip {cluster_name}", "dim"))

   498→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   499→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   500→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   501→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   502→
   503→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   504→    clusters sort by queue position.
   505→
   506→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   507→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   508→    """
   509→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   510→
   511→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   512→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   513→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   514→
   515→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   516→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   517→        clusters.items(),
   518→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   519→    )
   520→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   521→
   522→
   523→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   524→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   525→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   526→    active: str | None,
   527→) -> None:
   528→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   529→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   530→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   531→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)
   532→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   533→    print()
   534→    dep_header = f"  {'Dep':>3}" if has_dep else ""
   535→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Pri':>3}{dep_header}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   536→    dep_sep = f"  {'─'*3}" if has_dep else ""
   537→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*3}{dep_sep}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*40}"
   538→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   539→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   540→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   541→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   542→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   543→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   544→        pri_str = str(priority) if priority is not None else "—"
   545→        dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   546→        dep_str = f"  {dep_order:>3}" if has_dep and dep_order is not None else ("  {:>3}".format("—") if has_dep else "")
   547→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   548→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   549→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   550→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   551→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   552→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   553→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   554→        desc_truncated = (desc[:39] + "…") if len(desc) > 40 else desc
   555→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   556→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   557→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {pri_str:>3}{dep_str}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   558→    print()
   559→
   560→
   561→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   562→    plan = load_plan()
   563→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   564→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   565→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   566→    missing_steps: bool = getattr(args, "missing_steps", False)
   567→
   568→    if not clusters:
   569→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   570→        return
   571→
   572→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   573→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   574→
   575→    if missing_steps:
   576→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.stage_helpers import _unenriched_clusters
   577→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   578→        if not gaps:
   579→            print(colorize("  All clusters have action steps.", "green"))
   580→            return
   581→        print(colorize(f"  {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need action steps:", "bold"))
   582→        for name, missing in gaps:
   583→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   584→        print()
   585→        print(colorize("  Fix with:", "dim"))
   586→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   587→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "step title" --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   588→        return
   589→
   590→    if verbose:
   591→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   592→        return
   593→
   594→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   595→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   596→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   597→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   598→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   599→        pri_tag = f" [P{priority}]" if priority is not None else ""
   600→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   601→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   602→        marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   603→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   604→        auto_tag = " [auto]" if cluster.get("auto") else ""
   605→        print(f"    {pos_str:>5} {pri_tag} {name}: {member_count} items{auto_tag}{desc_str}{marker}")
   606→
